events.title: FOSS: an immersive live audiovisual experience
events.description:
FOSS is an immersive live audiovisual experience where electronic music, cinematic visuals, and cutting-edge technology converge. Created by Grammy-nominated pianist and composer Romain Collin and producer/electronic musician Jeremy Loucas, the performance grew from Collin’s six-month artistic retreat in the remote Icelandic highlands, where silence, vast landscapes, and isolation inspired a striking new creative vision.

Performed entirely live using modular synthesizers, tape machines, keyboards, and custom analog instruments—with no pre-recorded tracks—FOSS surrounds audiences with richly layered ambient soundscapes, projection-mapped visuals, and a quadraphonic sound system. The result is a mesmerizing, genre-defying performance that blurs the boundaries between music, film, nature, and technology.

Learn more at fossfossfoss.com

events.title: Gummo
events.description:
Harmony Korine’s debut feature is an audacious, lyrical evocation of America’s rural underbelly, and an elegy in the southern-gothic tradition of William Faulkner and William Eggleston. Shot in Korine’s native Nashville—standing in for the tornado-ravaged Xenia, Ohio—the rough-hewn film follows two young friends, Tummler and Solomon, as they ride around town, huffing glue and hunting stray cats, their every local encounter charged with vaudevillian anarchy as well as deep pathos. At once transgressive and empathetic, disturbing and undeniably beautiful, Gummo is a one-of-a-kind portrait of angelic and devilish souls caught in a cultural void, circumscribed by poverty and the depleted, alienated spiritual life of late-twentieth-century America.

This film can be used with loyalty cards or our 2026 annual CinemaSFBay passes

As a girl growing up in the 90s, everyone seemed to know Rebecca had Autism Spectrum Disorder except for her! And her parents! However, one thing was crystal clear: she had no idea how to “act normal.” This show will cover Rebecca's hilarious journey of self-exploration and her lifelong struggle to adapt, including at one point literally googling “how to act normal” and landing on the pinnacle of the ‘00s internet: WikiHow.
ABOUT REBECCA
Rebecca Kaplan is an adorably awkward standup comedian. Her acerbic wit and relatable insights have entertained crowds all over the world. She's appeared on the Late Show with David Letterman and has been featured on SiriusXM, NPR, and the front page of WorldStarHipHop. She lives in NYC, where she co-hosts the Bad Fan Fic podcast. Follow her on all social media at @RebeccaTKaplan to check out her clips.

events.address: 50 Mark West Springs Road, Santa Rosa, CA, 95403
events.description:
Froggy 92.9 celebrates its 30th birthday with a high-energy country celebration featuring Sony Music Nashville’s Corey Kent. Kent brings his signature blend of Oklahoma grit, country soul and rebel rock energy to the stage for a performance built on conviction, powerhouse vocals and hard-earned momentum. Rising from the dancehalls and dive bars of Bixby, Oklahoma, Kent has carved his own lane in country music with a sound influenced by Bruce Springsteen and Creedence Clearwater Revival as much as George Strait and Brooks & Dunn. His journey has been defined by perseverance, from early Nashville setbacks to a breakout run that now includes two No. 1 country radio hits, the 3X Platinum “Wild As Her,” the Gold-certified “This Heart,” Platinum-certified “Something’s Gonna Kill Me” and more than one billion career streams. With his latest album, Heartland Rock and Roll, Kent leans fully into the sound that sets him apart: smoky vocals, small-town storytelling, country-rock intensity and a deep sense of gratitude earned through the slow build.

Opening the celebration is Max Vogel, a Windsor-based country artist known for honest storytelling, strong melodies and a modern take on traditional country roots. Together, Corey Kent and Max Vogel deliver a spirited night of music that blends national country star power with local Sonoma County energy. Join us in celebrating Froggy’s 30th birthday with a concert you won’t want to miss!

events.title: An Evening with Mike Kuchar
events.description:
The vibrant, poetic and wild works of Mike Kuchar have inspired generations of filmmakers and artists with their wickedly perverse parodies of pop-culture and abundant creativity. From early 8 mm films made with his twin brother George Kuchar featuring friends from their Bronx neighbourhood to the underground sci-fi extravaganza Sins of the Fleshapoids 1965, his films take the language of Hollywood and make it so ‘overblown it’s glorious’. In the 1990s Mike Kuchar embraced video with the same transformative passion that he brought to his early 8 mm films, and created a vast body of work ranging from delirious teleplays to recent digital fantasies, displaying a unique creative sensibility. Relishing the possibilities of the most minuscule budgets his films are radiant and lurid in equal measure, celebrating human creativity with an undiminished passion and humor for over 50 years.

Program:

Age of Awareness: A mind blowing journey into the New Age

Forward Fancies: Unbridled poets recites audacious poems

Marisa Anderson's music transcends borders. The topography of her work interrogates the intersections of artistry and expression with form and tradition. A singular guitarist and voracious musical collaborator, Anderson crafts pieces bursting with equal parts reverence and curiosity, contouring familiar shapes into work that is wholly her own.

The Anthology of UnAmerican Folk Music is a collection of nearly one thousand songs culled from the private record collection of the late Harry Smith. Assembled by Anderson after a chance encounter led to an opportunity to study and explore this treasure trove of music, the Anthology focuses on music from places that the United States has been in conflict with since 1970: Southeast Asia, the USSR and the Arabic and Islamic regions of the world. In Volume 1 Anderson presents her own deeply personal iterations of nine songs from the Anthology. Composed, transcribed and arranged through a process of trial and error, deep listening and research, Anderson charts a musical course from Afghanistan to Vietnam via Yemen, Cambodia and Turkmenistan.

events.title: The Art of Succulent Terrariums: A Hands-On Workshop
events.description:
Imagine having your very own little world that's exactly how you want it to be. A tiny pocket dimension you can escape to when life gets stressful or you just need a dose of zen. Your very own ecosystem, created with your own two hands. No, this isn't some creator god fantasy. It's our Terrarium Workshop.

Speaking from experience, having some greenery around the house definitely boosts my mood, and taking care of it is its own kind of satisfaction. A terrarium is that feeling, but twice over. It's a tiny plant oasis that you get to design however you like and then tend to like some sort of benevolent domestic plant deity.

What's even cooler is that terrariums exist because of a happy accident that helped shape the modern world.
In 1829, a London physician named Nathaniel Bagshaw Ward sealed a moth chrysalis inside a glass bottle and accidentally changed the way plants traveled around the world. His little experiment led to the invention of the Wardian case, a glass container that helped smuggle tea out of China, launch the global rubber trade (historically important, even if that part didn't exactly age well), and eventually bring the Cavendish banana to grocery stores everywhere.

Fast forward a couple hundred years, and we're using the same basic idea for something a little less world-changing, but arguably more fun. In this workshop, you'll build a thriving little desert in glass that can happily live on your windowsill for years with very little effort.

This year’s Litquake festival will take place October 8th-24th! For more information about Litquake’s festival and year-round programs, visit litquake.org.

The series wherein famous authors choose a film that intersects with their artistic obsessions.

Andrew Sean Greer is a Pulitzer Prize winning author whose humor, warmth, and candor could ignite a room from the page. For this special Litquake Festival installment, Greer introduces Amarcord, the dramatic comedy directed by Federico Fellini for this special matinee.

Fellini recreates his hometown of Rimini in this carnivalesque film, where the director satirizes his childhood. Time magazine says: “Fellini is so bountiful with incident and observation that he makes most other filmmakers seem stingy.” Winner of an Academy Award for best foreign-language film, Amarcord remains one of the director’s best-loved creations, beautifully weaving together Giuseppe Rottuno’s colorful cinematography, Danilo Donati’s extravagant costumes and sets, and Nino Rota’s nostalgia-tinged score.

Greer’s Villa Coco reaches a magical and madcap tone that is in kin with this Fellini film. In Villa Coco, a young man takes an unspecified job with a charismatic elderly Baronessa at her crumbling villa in the Tuscan hills. David Sedaris says: “No one writing in English is funnier or more charming than Andrew Greer.”

events.description:

You know, tropes like the mean popular girl, the incredibly winsome new kid, the snarky outsiders, the handsome jock who always turns out to be a d-bag. Well, THE CRAFT takes all of those vital elements and throws in some black magic to create a thoroughly entertaining Gen-X witch's brew.

events.title: Creative Health Cartography: Collage Mapping and Guided Storytelling Workshop
events.description:
Are you feeling creatively blocked?
Has your health altered the way you work in ways you can’t quite pinpoint?

This workshop is for you.

You’ll work with a variety of collage materials, all provided, alongside guided prompts and reflection that move at a pace built for the room. There will be some story sharing woven throughout, always optional, and plenty of spaciousness to follow your own creative terrain rather than anyone else’s timeline.

You’ll be free to go as deep as feels right, and no deeper. To take a break if you need one. To skip anything that doesn’t feel like yours to do that day, or to sit with a blank page if that’s what’s true for you in the moment. You are the only one who knows what you actually need, and we trust that.

Come with whatever is true for you right now. That will be enough.

You’ll leave with a clearer picture of your own creative terrain: a better sense of what the block actually is, real confidence in the strengths and adaptations you’ve already built, and one small idea for how to move forward.

Group is kept intentionally small so space is very limited. Book today.

events.description:
The 29th United Nations Association Film Festival presents free programming for kids on Saturday, Oct. 17, in Palo Alto, featuring two short documentaries.

The program opens with the world premiere of "The Fixer," a 12-minute stop-motion documentary from local filmmakers Mimi Chakarova and Lydia Chávez. The film follows a 10-year-old girl determined to fix what is broken in a fragile world.

The program continues with "Under the Canopy," directed by Michal Krawczyk. Set in Colombia’s Andean-Amazon Piedmont, the documentary follows a community-led effort to map biodiversity and restore forests while preserving Indigenous ecological knowledge.

**Admission is free.** This special UNAFF & Kids Program offers an opportunity to see two short documentaries suitable for all audiences. The 29th UNAFF runs Oct. 15-25, 2026, with the theme “Passion for Change.” The festival features films addressing human rights issues, including the environment, women’s rights, racism and peace, and engages audiences throughout the Bay Area.

More info at unaff.org.

FREE show with the legendary Joe Bataan in San Francisco, only at Yerba Buena Gardens Festival! With opening set from MeloDious and pre-show music from KALW DJ Marcus.

Festival favorite Joe Bataan, a Latin music legend since the mid-1960s, returns to the Gardens for his third performance in the past four years. He made an indelible mark as one of the early stars of Fania Records with a seductive combination of doo-wop vocals and boogaloo, one of the era’s defining sounds. Born Bataan Nitollano to a Filipino father and African-American mother and raised in Spanish Harlem, he is the father of the Latin soul sound, crooning hits like “Gypsy Woman” and “Ordinary Guy.” But Bataan never stayed in one groove for long. He went on to expand his sound in the ’70s with his Ghetto Records releases, co-coining the apt moniker “salsoul,” though he adapted to changing currents at the end of the decade with forays into disco and hip-hop (scoring the early rap hit “Rap-O Clap-O” in 1979). Stepping back from performing in the early ‘80s, he largely disappeared from the scene while working as a youth counselor in detention facilities. It’s a dramatic story that he recounts with humor and searing detail in his 2024 memoir Streetology: The Legacy of the Afro-Filipino, King of Latin Soul. Since returning to music in 2005, he’s reclaimed his crown and is still going strong in his 80s, a...

events.description:
Strange things are afoot in Bad City. The Iranian ghost town, home to prostitutes, junkies, pimps, and other sordid souls, is a place that reeks of death and hopelessness, where a lonely vampire is stalking the towns most unsavory inhabitants. But when boy meets girl, an unusual love story begins to blossom...blood red.

The first Iranian Vampire Western, Ana Lily Amirpour's debut feature A Girl Walks Home Alone at Night basks in the sheer pleasure of pulp. A joyful mash-up of genre, archetype and iconography, its prolific influences span spaghetti westerns, graphic novels, horror films, and the Iranian New Wave. Amped by a mix of Iranian rock, techno and Morricone-inspired riffs, its airy, anamorphic, black-and-white aesthetic and artfully drawn-out scenes combine the simmering tension of Sergio Leone with the surrealism of David Lynch.

events.description:
When the Marquis d’Urfé, a noble emissary of the King of France, is attacked and abandoned in the remote countryside, he finds refuge at an eerie, isolated manor. events.address: 401 Van Ness Ave, San Francisco, CA, 94102
events.description:
Theatre Flamenco celebrates its 60th anniversary home season, 'De Ayer a Hoy / From Yesterday to Today,' on Saturday, October 17 at Herbst Theater in San Francisco. The program will honor the legacy of Founder Adela Clara as well as Miguel Santos, the company's first artistic director, whose vision inspired an enduring tradition of flamenco in the San Francisco Bay Area. Both Clara and Santos recently passed away.

Among the luminaries who will perform is Cristina Hall, a flamenco artist originally from San Francisco who has lived in Seville for more than 20 years. She will perform a new work commissioned for the occasion.

Adrian Santana, a dancer from Malaga, Spain, will also perform. With a tribute to Theatre Flamenco's inaugural artistic director, Santana has chosen to reimagine Miguel Santos's 'Zapateado/Farruca' from 1989. Santana will also join Zertuche in a new duet honoring the founder of Theatre Flamenco.

Additional guest artists include Roberto Aguilar, Krista Bloom, Gina Giammanco, Nevarez Encinias, Aldo Ruiz, Nol Simonse and Lauren Smiley.

Guest musicians include Diego Amado Jr., singer and multi-instrumentalist from Seville, Spain; Amparo Heredia, a singer based in Granada, Spain; electronic musician Pascual Martinez; and guitarist Jesse Torre, based in the Bay Area.

The program will feature a total of nine works, including three premieres and six reimagined pieces from Theatre Flamenco's repertoire.

events.title: Dean Evans: Les Pervers - Flop Fest!
events.description:
Renowned Clown and Mime artist Dean Evans presents a series of darkly comedic personas, one after another, in a tour de force of physical transformation. Dean slips between an Edgar Allan Poe–esque horror writer, a retired showgirl from Branson Missouri, a dying Mime gasping out one last performance, and an entity simply known as "Slime Rat" and more. Evans takes us on a tour of the dark recesses of their clown brain in this hour long perverse Spoon River Anthology.
Created & Performed by Dean Evans.

Artist Bio
Dean Evans is an award-winning performer, director, and master physical theater artist. Named one of the top 50 ‘players’ by New City magazine Dean tours internationally as a solo artist and has performed professionally with the Second City, iO, the Goodman, Cirque du Soleil and more. Dean was an ensemble member of the iconic performance art troop the Neo-Futurists in Chicago. Dean has directed many troops including Slowdance, iL Fungo. the Nonsemble, and Mil Grus who had an off-broadway run in NYC in 2019. Dean’s alter ego, Honeybuns, has enjoyed their own career performing in NYC, Chicago, Moscow, Ireland, Austin, Boston, Portland and Los Angeles. Dean has created over a dozen full-length theatrical productions, 3 full-length circuses, and dozens of comedic characters. They have appeared on NBC, AMC, TBS, Netflix, The Onion, and Russia’s минута славы. Dean also writes & directs really cool films.

events.title: Jessie Ware
events.description:
Goldenvoice Presents
The Superbloom Tour 2026
Jessie Ware
with Dhruv

Saturday, October 17 | The Warfield

Mercury Prize and 6-time BRIT nominated singer and songwriter Jessie Ware returns with a phenomenal new album that establishes why Ware is one of the most revered, admired and loved voices at the forefront of British Pop music. That! Feels Good! is the follow-up to Ware’s fourth studio album, 2020’s What’s Your Pleasure. There’s a delicious feeling of freedom to be found throughout Jessie Ware’s new album That! Feels Good! It’s the sound of a person letting loose and letting go and encouraging everyone else to do the same. This blissfully joyful record, underscored by a frankly sensational vocal from Ware, radiates self-determination, boundless energy, supremely good vibes and a generosity of spirit. And groove. So. Much. Groove. Yet That! Feels Good! also resounds with an ebullient ease; an unforced and unhurried spirit runs throughout each and every one of the 10 tracks.

events.title: Planet of the Vampires
events.description:
A Close Encounter of the Undead Kind! In this otherworldly tour de force of sci-fi thrills and Gothic chills, space travelers intercept a mysterious distress call from a distant world. Is it a desperate cry for helpor something far more sinister? After landing on the shadowy planet, the crew members clash with a horde of disembodied, soul-snatching aliens with a diabolical plan beyond their worst nightmares! A dazzling mixture of nerve-shredding suspense, eye-popping science fiction and full-blooded horror from the maestro of the macabre, Mario Bava (Black Sunday, Black Sabbath), Planet of the Vampires inspired decades of space-age shockers and now proudly stands as one of the most electrifying, visually stunning cult classics from Italian cinema’s golden age.

Playing as part of the International Vampire Film Fest at the Balboa on Saturday, October 17. Individual tickets and $30 day passes on sale now.

events.price_text: $0-$20 sliding scale, no one turned away
events.description:
BECAUSE I HAVE TO is a discussion series featuring Bay Area artists, writers, musicians, chefs, and creators who work across multiple artistic and creative mediums, against the grain of their professional lives, alongside it, or within it. Hosted by Jeff Wright, these conversations will delve into creative work in the modern age, the real whys that drive us to make it, how it intertwines with our lives, and what really makes it all possible.

BIHT #1 will feature Amar Lal and Paolo Bicchieri. If you’re in the Bay Area, their fingerprints are probably already on something familiar to you, due to their presence and commitment to culture and creative work here. Professionally, Amar is fine-tuning and refining songs we listen to at his Oakland studio every day. He also creates visual works of art to express sound, as noted in his latest book, Practicing Joy. Paolo’s creative writing can be found in any given news outlet, narrating underrepresented projects, or throughout his handful of published poetry works. He also organizes community events to uplift local poets, writers, and up-and-coming chefs through Kitchen Table. All of this work takes perseverance, the right settings, creative discipline, and much more that we are set to discuss in the first edition of BECAUSE I HAVE TO.

events.description:
The David Brower Center | 2150 Allston Way, Berkeley (between Oxford and Schattuck) 12-5pm

Birding Field Trips | Various Parks Around Berkeley 8am-5pm

Free | Family-Friendly | All Ages

Every bird holds a memory. Every memory holds a meaning. Across different cultures and communities, across time and space, birds have played a significant role in shaping our understanding of the world, ourselves, and our relationship in nature.
On Sunday, October 18th, this year’s Berkeley Bird Festival invites you to celebrate our incredible birdlife here in the Bay Area through the theme of “Myth and Memories”.
Get outside and witness the birds and our shared environment. Engage with the Myth of the Flying Africans.
Fold a crane for peace and longevity. Hear the story of SF’s Wild Parrots. Watch the street “split the sky” through a dance inspired by migration. Listen to the science behind wildlife and remember, every feather, past and present, is a portal to a world where all of us thrive.
This festival brings science, art, and culture under its wing to inspire our collective imagination and action in protecting birds and our environment. We hope you’ll join us whether you're bird-curious or a long-time advocate.
Register in advance to attend a trip, or gather your flock, swoop in, and dive into a world of birds, Myth and Memory.

Film Director and Writer Bobby Buccallato shares his documentary film debut of Carter Country, which follows the two-year journey of America’s most unlikely Presidential candidate Jimmy Carter and his small town that followed him every step of the way.

This documentary seeks to capture the forgotten spirit of 1976, the last great Presidential election of the 20th century, when a small town in Georgia suddenly became the political capital of the world. This documentary is not the latest retelling of Jimmy Carter. It is the first telling of the community (his community) and their collective efforts that managed to lift up one of their own into The White House.

events.title: Spotlight Sundays: Roadsongs for Dorothea Lange
events.description:
For this month’s Spotlight Sunday join us for a live production of Last West: Roadsongs for Dorothea Lange, an immersive one-hour play written by Tess Taylor and directed by Ciera Eis. Last West was born from OMCA’s archive of Lange’s images and notebooks and returns to bring this legendary Bay Area photographer’s stories to life. We will travel with Lange as actors perform the journey outlined in her road journals and oral histories, and witness again the California we experience today. Set against a stunning projected backdrop of Lange’s photographs, this offering is a meditation on witness, migration, and time.

This production is a culmination of a weekend of programming centering and celebrating Dorothea Lange’s life and work. Kick off the weekend on Friday, October 16, 5:30–7:30pm with a free public symposium at UC Berkeley’s Northgate Hall, featuring Last West creator Tess Taylor and Ken Light, UC Berkeley Professor of Photojournalism. Saturday, October 17, 1-3pm join Last West actors from the production in an intimate day of teasers with pop up monologues in OMCA’s Galleries of Art and History right alongside Lange’s displays. Free with gallery admission.

Explore more of Lange’s work in our latest special exhibition, BeHere / 1942: A New Lens on the Japanese American Incarceration, an augmented reality (AR) experience that brings new context to Lange’s iconic 1942 photographs. We invite you to join us for this special weekend of programming and experience Lange’s wor...

events.title: United Nations Association Film Festival | Free Shorts Program
events.description:
The 29th United Nations Association Film Festival presents a free shorts program on Sunday, Oct. 18, in Palo Alto, featuring three documentaries that explore wildlife conservation, wrongful incarceration, and the global impact of cryptocurrency.

The program opens with "Crossing the Divide," directed and produced by local filmmaker Talia Frank. The 11-minute documentary examines how roads fragment wildlife habitats and explores the potential of wildlife crossings to restore animal movement and strengthen ecosystems.

Next is "The Dreaming Game," directed and produced by Jordan Salvatoriello. The film follows 70-year-old Raymond Gaines, a Boston native and lifelong baseball fan, as he returns to Fenway Park after spending 47 years in prison for a murder he did not commit. As he awaits a decision on his case, Gaines works to rebuild his life and pursue his long-sought freedom.

The program concludes with "The Market and the Monkey’s Paw," directed and produced by "Graham New, Leo Safir, and Oliver Richards. Set in El Salvador, the documentary explores the country’s adoption of Bitcoin as legal tender through the perspectives of market vendors, educators and community members, examining questions of economic inclusion, tourism, gentrification and digital finance.

**Admission is free.** The special program from UNAFF offers an opportunity to see three short documentaries and discover the work of filmmakers from the Bay Area and beyond. UNAFF runs Oct. 15–25, 2026, with the theme...

events.title: A Tale of Two Sisters
events.description: If you think about it long enough, anything can be supernatural – your toothbrush, a pair of sneakers, or your parents. That’s what makes A TALE OF TWO SISTERS so terrifying. Sisters Soo-mi and Soo-yeon arrive at their father’s country home to spend some quality time with their new stepmother. But there’s trouble in paradise. For proof, check out the severed hands that live in a kitchen cabinet. The first Korean horror movie to be distributed in America, A TALE OF TWO SISTERS is a beautiful hallucinogen. It’s quiet, violent, and visually stunning, feeling like a Korean version of THE SHINING as filtered through the adolescent pre-angst of a Judy Blume novel if Judy Blume was secretly a demon. You’ll never see another haunted house movie like this one – and you’ll never forget it. (Joseph A. Ziemba)

events.title: Litquake Presents Menopause Extravaganza: The Science and Culture of a Subject No One Used to Want to Talk About
events.description:
Menopause Extravaganza: The Science and Culture of a Subject No One Used to Want to Talk About

Sunday, October 18, 2026

Doors: 2:30 PM

All Ages

Seated event

View our FAQ page for more info, or contact us at [email protected] with any accommodation requests.

Menopause, a natural consequence of aging, has for centuries been alternately ignored and belittled, seen mostly through a male lens of bafflement, repugnance, and boilerplate misogyny. Now, however, a growing body of women and their doctors are rejecting this traditional view, developing new therapies and strategies as well as ways to appreciate the new freedoms it can offer.

This energizing (and overdue) afternoon features Dr. Louann Brizendine, author of The Female Brain, reading from her forthcoming Your Brain on Menopause and joining other panelists in a conversation led by Keli Dailey: Dr. Sarah Isquick (a colleague of Dr. Sally Greenwald, featured in the recent New Yorker article “The Billionaires’ Vagina Club”), psychiatrist Dr. Alecia Greenlee, and menopause doula Lasara Firefox Allen, author of Genderqueer Menopause.

Select performers from The Menopause Monologues® will kick off the event. Bring your friends for a conversation-sparking afternoon.

events.title: Dinosaur Jr.
events.description:
Another Planet Entertainment presents
Dinosaur Jr.

Sunday, October 18 | The Castro

Finally! The sixth studio album Dinosaur Jr. have recorded in the 20 years since their triumphal rebirth. There have been several live and/or closet cleaning collections to keep us punters sated for the five years since Sweep It Into Space, but there is nothing quite like having a full slab of new Dino tunes to fry your ears. And There Near has all knobs set to Extra Crispy.

Created in short, intense bursts over the course of a year at Amherst’s Bisquiteen Studio, There Near was recorded almost entirely by Dino’s core trio — king of the thunder tubs, Murph, human tornado Lou Barlow on bass/vocals and the inimitable J Mascis on guitar/vocals — with a bit of piano and organ work by local master musician, Ken Mauri. And the album roars from start to finish.

Trying to define the essence of Dino’s sound is never easy. It’s an instantly recognizable blend of loose vocals, sharp guitars and an animalistic rhythm section, but these parts combine into a whole far more magical and exciting than its components. In strict rock-write terms, you might call the approach “post-core power balladeering,” but what use is that? Dinosaur Jr. invented their formula for noise/pop jiggering around the same time Husker Dü were trying out some of the same ideas, all of which got made popular by a band they inspired called Nirvana. But that’s an old and much-told tale.

MUNA is a Los Angeles-based indie pop trio who met at USC's Thornton School of Music in 2013 and have since grown into one of indie pop's most vital and electrifying acts. A touchstone for LGBTQ+ audiences, they build hook-driven, emotionally candid worlds that drench electronics, post-punk, synth-pop, and new wave in metallic sheen while carrying a brooding melancholy that undercuts the hedonistic highs. Their 2022 self-titled album earned them Band of the Year from Consequence of Sound, year-end list placement from Billboard, Rolling Stone, and TIME, and slots opening for both Harry Styles and Taylor Swift on their respective tours. Now, with their forthcoming album Dancing On The Wall, MUNA channel the raw, anxious energy of political tension, millennial precarity, and personal heartache into a fast-paced, hard-edged dance pop record that is intimate, spectacular, socially conscious, and joyful all at once.

She Wants Revenge, the dark-alternative duo who first exploded onto the scene with the 2005 hit, “Tear You Apart”, are back with a new song, festival appearances, a new lineup, and a massive global audience hungry for the 3rd wave gothic rock they ushered in 2up and down decades before.

Soon they were opening for Depeche Mode, The Psychedelic Furs, Placebo, co-headlining with Peter Murphy of Bauhaus, headlining Coachella alongside Daft Punk, and in constant rotation on alternative rock across the country. - Hemming jeans, stretch fabrics, and delicate sheers

- Repairing seams

- Sewing on buttons

- Simple mending techniques

During class, you will practice using a selection of different fabrics. We also encourage you to bring a few items of your own to work on if you like. Your instructor will guide you through all hemming and repair techniques but will not directly mend your selected items. That's where you come in!! Each student will gain a working knowledge of each hemming and repair techniques, as well as the opportunity to work on 1-2 pieces from home.

Please Note: This is a beginner-friendly class that does not require prior hand or machine sewing knowledge. However, this would not be a replacement for one of our other Sewing 101 or Sewing Bootcamp classes, which give a more complete introduction to using sewing machines. Also, this class will not cover replacing / repairing zippers, as that's a whole 'nother thing!!

Supplies Needed: All materials for practice are provided so you can try out several techniques on different types of fabric. You may bring a few pieces from home...

Across his career, Shakey Graves—a.k.a. the performance moniker of Austin, Texas-born Alejandro Rose-Garcia—has intentionally created thrilling musical adventures tailored to each fan: burning CDs and putting them in personalized decorated bags; building intricate scavenger hunts that send fans in search of unique tapes; and Bandcamp-exclusive releases.

“The fans and musicians that really resonate with me—and the inexplicable ways that I find things that I like—are usually entirely through randomness and chaos and accident,” Rose-Garcia says. “I’ve always been on this quest to make people feel like my own music is a choose your own adventure.”

In 2024 Rose-Garcia celebrated the ten year anniversary of his And The War Came album with a special 10 Year Anniversary Edition release featuring never before heard demos and b-sides from the recording process and inviting fans to enter the long-since abandoned Music House.

His story continues to unfold, but Shakey Graves Is Still A Gentleman From Texas.

events.title: Bat Week Screening of 'The Invisible Mammal'
events.description:
Award-winning documentary highlights global bat extinction crisis

The Citizens Environmental Council invites you to a free screening of an award-winning documentary highlighting the fight to save North American bats on Wednesday, October 21, from 6 to 8 p.m. at the Burlingame Community Center at 850 Burlingame Ave. in Burlingame. There is no charge for admission, but pre-registration is required. Watch the trailer below!

Just in time for Halloween - and Bat Week! - “The Invisible Mammal” focuses on the plight of several species of North American bats now at risk because of a deadly fungal disease called White-nose Syndrome (WNS) and a team of women biologists determined to rescue these rapidly vanishing species. After a screening of the 90-minute film, filmmaker Kristin Tièche will offer insights and answer questions about a strategy called Operation Fat Bat, pioneered by women scientists, that could rebuild healthy bat populations across North America.

Bats save U.S. agriculture billions of dollars in pesticide use each year, and the decline of bat populations is linked to an increase in infant mortality where these pesticides are used. Since 2006, WNS has decimated bat populations across 42 states and Canada, killing millions of bats.

The Citizens Environmental Council’s mission is to champion regional sustainability through education, advocate for environmental and climate policies, and empower young environmental leaders. For more information, visit cecburlingame.org...

events.title: Presentation: Eyewitness to the Resistance
events.description:
Indivisible SF presents a panel of local photojournalists from Pro Bono Photo and other news organizations who share selections from their portfolios and discuss the role photojournalism plays in documenting protest, civic action and pro-democracy movements.

From the civil rights and voting rights movements of the 1960s to today's social justice actions, the San Francisco Bay Area has long been a significant site of protest and civil disobedience. Who documents these fleeting moments of protest and civic action? Local photojournalists share their experiences covering pro-democracy movements and street demonstrations throughout the Bay Area.

Hear firsthand accounts from photographers documenting recent protests and demonstrations, view a curated projection of their work and engage directly with the panelists during an audience Q&A.

Pop-Up Gallery: A selection of photographs by participating photojournalists will be displayed alongside historical protest photography from SFPL collections, connecting contemporary documentation of Bay Area demonstrations with the Library's photographic record of protest and civic action. The display will be on view on the 4th Floor of the Main Library from Sept. 17-Dec. 31.

Free

Presented by San Francisco Public Library

events.title: Rakim
events.description:
In the history of Hip-Hop, few artists have had as great an impact on the development and progression of the art form's lyrical style as Rakim Allah. Universally referenced as one of the Masters of the Microphone and an influence and inspiration to his peers and followers alike, Rakim first exploded onto the scene with the release of the iconic Eric B. is President in 1986 with long-time collaborator Eric B. The single marked a turning point in the Rap world – raising the bar for future emcees and revolutionizing the way rhymes are delivered to this day. No serious discussion of the music’s greatest performers is held without a deferential accounting of his achievements, and no serious rap artist grips a microphone without channeling some of his legend.

Rakim’s intricately intellectual lyrics draw their force from his worldly experience, inner faith, and progressive contemplation; his liquid and seemingly effortless delivery – often imitated but still unrivaled – from a fire fueled by a deep understanding of not just Hip-Hop, but also the Jazz and R&B influences that have surrounded his family since his youth. His recordings – including the all-time classics Paid In Full, Follow the Leader and The 18th Letter - have sold in the multi-millions worldwide. Billboard, Rolling Stone, MTV, and a host of others consistently refer to Paid in Full as “the greatest Hip-Hop album of all time” – a claim that is often repeated in audience polls. This informal drop-in experience is an opportunity for visitors to share their personal reflections with and ask questions of our enthusiastic and knowledgeable volunteer facilitators.

Visitors can find Gallery Chatters—wearing their blue “Let’s Chat” shirts—and floating between OMCA’s Galleries of California Art, History, Natural Science, and the Great Hall during Friday Nights (April-Oct), ThursDates (Jan-March), and our community celebrations, including Lunar New Year, Día de los Muertos, and Juneteenth (hours vary).

Whether you’re curious about something on view or excited to reflect on your own experiences, Gallery Chatters are here to help spark conversation and connection. Your stories matter at OMCA—just say hello to start exploring together.

OMCA Members have access to special Member Tours every second Saturday of the month from noon to 1 pm.

events.title: In Their Name: Día de Los Muertos 2026
events.description:
Get your tickets to the opening and exhibition unveiling of SOMArts' "In Their Name: Día de Los Muertos 2026"! The evening features a Día de los Muertos inspired artist market with local vendors and makers, along with a special performance by Las Hijas de la Madre.

Curated by Bridgètt Rex and Rio Yañez, "In Their Name: Dia de Los Muertos 2026" cherishes the ancestral memory, love, and devotion carried and embodied by mother figures across generations. In keeping with the tradition of Día de los Muertos, the exhibition also includes personal altars dedicated to loved ones who have passed.

About Las Hijas de la Madre

Las Hijas de la Madre are a queer Chicanx feminist punk band featuring Amalia Ortiz (lyricist and lead singer), Errezeta (lead guitar, vocals), Lilith Tijerina (bass, vocals), Sarah Tijerina (vocals, keyboard), Dr. Kip Austin Hinton (rhythm guitar and musical direction), and Joaquin Muerte (drums).

Fronted by Amalia Ortiz, an American Book Award winner for Oral Literature, Las Hijas de la Madre center Tejana voices and explore the connection between Chicanx rasquachismo and the DIY ethos of punk. Through an intersectional feminist lens, they radically re-envision a historically white, male expression of punk.

The Golden Casket heralds another new chapter in the GRAMMY® Award-nominated multi platinum band’s unpredictable evolution. Produced with Dave Sardy and Jacknife Lee in Los Angeles and in Modest Mouse’s studio in Portland, the album hovers in the liminal space between raw punk power and experimental studio science, frontman Isaac Brock explores themes ranging from the degradation of our psychic landscapes and invisible technology, to fatherhood. Los Vega Son Jarocho
Friday, October 23 | The Freight

Los Vega is a traditional son jarocho group that has been dedicated to the performance, dissemination, and promotion of this musical genre for 20 years. Their music is characterized by the balance they achieve between their cultural roots and family heritage with musical quality and stage experience. They have participated in numerous cultural and artistic festivals in the country and abroad, in countries such as China, the United States, Canada, and Colombia. In 2018, they performed a show bringing together more than 20 renowned son jarocho artists to commemorate their 20th anniversary.

They have participated in various film recordings, one of them with the song "La Bruja" for the film "Frida," which was included in the soundtrack and was nominated for an Oscar in 2001. They were nominated for an Oscar in 2019 for the Lunas del Auditorio. That same year, they were invited to participate in the Tibetan Benefit Concert at Carnegie Hall in New York, conducted by renowned composer Philip Glass.

Their most recent participation in Circulart Colombia included a live showcase. Throughout their career, they have released five albums.

events.title: Nureyev
events.description:
The extraordinary story of an artist who not only transformed the world of ballet, but stood as a symbol of artistic freedom and individual self-determination.

Experience a live performance capture of the multi-award-winning ballet Nureyev, choreographed by Yuri Possokhov (San Francisco Ballet Choreographer in Residence) in collaboration with stage director Kirill Serebrennikov, with a score by composer Ilya Demutsky.

The production blends ballet, opera, and drama into a sweeping homage to one of the 20th century’s greatest dancers, tracing his rise in the Soviet Union, his dramatic defection to the West, his open expression of his homosexuality, and his enduring influence on Western ballet.

The ballet premiered at Russia’s Bolshoi Theatre in 2017 to widespread acclaim, but was permanently removed from its repertoire in 2022 under Russia’s expanded “gay propaganda” law. Staged by Staatsballett Berlin in 2026, marking the first time Nureyev had been performed outside of Russia, this live performance capture brings that landmark production to the screen.

Following the screening, join Nureyev composer Ilya Demutsky and co-stager Dana Genshaft for a live Q&A moderated by SFDFF Artistic Director Garen Scribner.

VIP ticket holders are invited to attend a photo opportunity and chat with the creative team immediately after the screening.

events.title: LIVE MUSIC: Izaak Opatz, Joe Kaplow
events.description:
Izaak Opatz

Izaak Opatz’s music has always been about longing, run through with nostalgia for the passed-by and out-of-reach. His first two albums, Mariachi Static and Extra Medium, were propelled by a longing for specific people and places, made relatable by wry humor, thoughtful simile and close observation.

More recently, he’s been writing songs that long for an alternative reality, for different possibilities than the short, doomed menu offered by our tech lords and the current kakistocracy failing to regulate them. Songs that push back against the coercive pressure to indulge in small conveniences at the expense of personal privacy, a 20th-century attention span and the steady drip of a monthly subscription:

I spend a lot of my time now, jumping through hoops / asking permission from a little screen convincing a robot that I’m not a robot / this future isn’t all it was cracked up to be

Joe Kaplow

My music comes from life’s moments — smelling 4 acres of freshly cut grass, watching the steam from a horse’s breath in the early morning, finally holding the neck of my guitar after holding bridles and worn wooden handles all day. 4000 acres of freshly burnt wildfire, watching the steam from the Pacific Ocean’s breath in the early morning, finally holding the neck of my guitar after clutching the worn steering wheel of the tour van all day.

Now my reality is in Bonny Doon, CA, where mountains meet the sea. I am in my recording studio, aptly named Hippie Cowboy, every day....

events.title: Liberation
events.description:
It's 1970s Ohio, and Lizzie has gathered a group of women in a rec center basement to change their lives and maybe the world. Decades later, Lizzie’s daughter delves into her mother’s history to find answers to the feminist revolution’s unanswered questions, reliving those necessary, messy, and impassioned meetings that asked: What does it mean for a woman to be free? Direct from its acclaimed Broadway run, Tony Award-winners Bess Wohl (Grand Horizons) and director Whitney White (Jaja's African Hair Braiding) bring ferocious wit and emotional precision to this intensely relevant and bitingly funny memory play about what we inherit, what we forget, and what we're still fighting to understand.

“An unadulterated pleasure. Powerfully moving and funny. When these women talk, we want to hear every word.” Critic’s Pick, The New York Times

Tyondai Braxton’s Splayed Werks is his fifth album and first full-length release since the recording of his 2018 symphonic work Telekinesis. A co-founder of acclaimed experimental rock project Battles, among many other achievements, Braxton’s work spans electroacoustic projects and contemporary composition.

—

“My philosophy on releasing music has changed a lot, but also my idea of what it means to be an artist. The important part of the artist’s job is to archive what you're doing—what you're excited about, what you're dealing with, what you're reacting against—putting that in a form that documents your life… At the moment, we're all looking out into the world, dealing with the helplessness in a time of war, media over-saturation. What's the role of the artist in that? I think the archiving of any particular creative idea in the moment is one of the most significant things an artist can do now. Things I previously thought were important—’this piece means so much to me,’ or ‘listen to how this chord arrived’—are actually much less so.”

Even at first blush, Splayed Werks, Tyondai Braxton’s fifth album, his first full-length release since the recording of his 2018 symphonic work, Telekinesis, reveals itself as unlike what came before and marks the beginning of a new chapter with UK label Erased Tapes. First off, there’s a lot...

events.description:
Think you can tell Fiji from Evian in a blind tasting? Know your Topo from your Pellegrino just from looking at the bubbles? Have you ever tried salty sparkling Spanish Vichy Catalan, or experienced the bizarre Borjomi from the Republic of Georgia?

Bottled waters differ dramatically in texture, minerality, carbonation, and finish. We’ll try lots of waters - some familiar and some super weird- and we’ll learn Why they taste the way they do in this alcohol-free experience.

We’ll start by blind tasting San Francisco tap to see if Hetch Hetchy is as heavenly as we’ve heard about. We’ll continue blind tasting bottled still waters from neutral to mineral-rich, then crack open a whole bunch of sparkling soda waters and go through them one-by-one.

This low-pressure and friendly tasting is perfect for curious drinkers, food lovers, coffee snobs, supertasters, sober folks, and people with strong opinions about H2O. Many attendees walk away with a new favorite brand. Skeptics leave convinced that water has plenty of flavor.

events.title: The Art of Kokedama: A Hands-On Workshop
events.description:
Are you into plants but have a deep desire to see them freed from the confines of a pot? Are you more of a natural beauty enjoyer than a curated-attempt-to-mimic-nature kind of person? Does the idea of hanging moss balls around your house put you in a good mood? If you answered yes to these, or even just one of them, our Kokedama Workshop is where you want to be.

Literally translating from Japanese to "moss ball" (not a very inventive name, but these are cool enough to forgive that), these green orbs are a method of growing plants in a ball of soil wrapped in moss instead of a traditional pot. Rather than hiding half the plant inside a container, kokedama wraps the roots and soil in a moss ball that eventually becomes part of the living display, blurring the line between container and plant.

Kokedama first took root (get it?) in Japan during the Edo period as an offshoot of bonsai. Instead of a traditional ceramic pot, the plant’s roots are tucked into a hand-shaped ball of specialized soil and wrapped in living moss, turning the plant itself into the centerpiece.

In Japanese culture, there is an aesthetic and philosophy called wabi-sabi that finds beauty in imperfection, impermanence, and simplicity. This is definitely a philosophy we can get behind. Maybe a little too much, but that’s beside the point. Kokedama fits nicely into wabi-sabi, and so does the life of the writer of this little blurb.

If you’re into imperfection, silver-lining Japanese philosophy, and hanging...

events.address: Yerba Buena Gardens covers two square city blocks bounded by Mission, Folsom, Third and Fourth Streets., San Francisco, CA, 94103
events.description:
Free RSVP

Few artists have appeared at the Festival more frequently than flutist, percussionist and arranger John Calloway. Whether he’s leading his own band, performing in the sextet of longtime creative partner John Santos, or directing the Latin Jazz Youth Ensemble of San Francisco, Calloway is a Bay Area icon who’s been at the center of the San Francisco Latin jazz scene for some five decades. But his latest and most personal project yet, the Afro-Filipino Jazz Project, takes his music in a new direction. Founded in 2022 as a creative, interactive space, the Project is intended to bring together Afro Filipinx, African American and Filipino American musicians to explore a broad range of musical styles, with a particular emphasis on jazz idioms, African American roots and traditional and folkloric Filipino music. It’s one component of the larger Afro-Filipino Project, a platform dedicated to highlighting and celebrating, individually and collectively, the art practices and artists of the African American and Filipino American communities whose contributions have profoundly shaped our nation’s artistic narrative. For this performance the AFJP features bass star Marcus Shelby, inveterately grooving drummer Deszon Claiborne, Latin jazz piano specialist Murray Low, saxophonist TJ Milan, Conrad Benedicto on kulintang, vocalist and dancer Ting Alvarez and guest vocalist Anna Maria Flechero.

WHEN MANILATOWN SWUNG: THE MANILA SERENADERS

What did Manilatown sound like when Kearny Street was alive with music?

Step into the sounds and stories of historic Manilatown for a special Club Mandalay: Music, Memory & Manilatown gathering featuring live jazz, archival photographs, family memories, and community Talk Story at the International Hotel Manilatown Center.

At the heart of the afternoon is Canuto Salaver, a drummer with the Manila Serenaders whose life was deeply connected to historic Manilatown and the I-Hotel. Members of the Salaver Family join guest interviewer Sabrina Oliveros to share family stories passed down about Canuto-his life around Kearny Street, his connection to the Bataan Cafe and Poolhall, and his years making music with the Manila Serenaders.

The musical lineage continues with Raymond Bambao, bassist with today's Manilatown Jazz Ensemble, whose grandfather and grand-uncles also played with the Manila Serenaders.

Throughout the afternoon, the Manilatown Jazz Ensemble brings these histories back into sound with live musical interludes inspired by the era, while photographs and materials from the Manilatown Archives and family collections bring the world of historic Manilatown into view.

Audience members will also be invited into the Talk Story-because the memories carried by our families and communities are part of how history lives.

And because history can be fun: Feeling festive? Come dressed in your 1930s-40s finest! Period-inspired attire...

events.title: One In A Million
events.description:
Post-screening Q&A with director Jack MacInnes & film subject, Israa!

Filmed over ten years, ONE IN A MILLION follows Israa from childhood to adulthood on an extraordinary journey from Syria to Germany — and back again. We first meet her at age 11 as she and her family are preparing to cross the Aegean Sea, risking everything in search of safety and a better life in Europe. What unfolds is a deeply personal chronicle of war, exile and heartbreak, as Israa grows up navigating adolescence, identity and belonging far from the home she was forced to leave. As Israa settles into life in Germany, new freedoms collide with the stabilizing pull of Syrian traditions, testing bonds and reshaping her sense of self.

Co-directed by Itab Azzam and Jack MacInnes, the film bears witness to the remarkable trust between filmmakers and family, following Israa and her loved ones across borders, cultures and shifting circumstances. An intimate and nuanced coming-of-age story, ONE IN A MILLION illuminates the complexities of the refugee experience while asking a universal question: what does it truly mean to call a place home?

events.title: “Castro on Fire”: A Queer Resistance Walking Tour by Unspeakable Vice
events.description:
LOCATION

4127 18th Street

San Francisco, CA 94114

ADMISSION

$35; Museum admission included in tour

RSVP and reserve tickets here

The GLBT Historical Society Museum is pleased to partner with Unspeakable Vice to offer a monthly walking tour focused on the history of LGBTQIA+ resistance in the Castro neighborhood. Created by tour guide, former senior adjunct professor, and practicing designer Shawn Sprockett, Unspeakable Vice began as a close look at the queer origins of San Francisco, traversing the city’s North Beach and Barbary Coast areas to trace the history through from 1770-1960. This new tour closes a three-part story, extending Sprockett’s detailed and engaging storytelling to the Castro neighborhood.

Ten years after the White Night riots, the police came back. Meet the trans man doctors turned away, the lesbians who ran the blood drives and wards, and the community that answered a plague and two police riots with the same refusal. This tour includes a free round at the Lookout, overlooking the neighborhood you've just walked.

events.description:
The power of words isn’t lost on longstanding Americana triumvirate The Devil Makes Three— Pete Bernhard, Lucia Turino, and Cooper McBean. For as much as they remain rooted in troubadour traditions of wandering folk, Delta blues, whiskey-soaked ragtime, and reckless rock ‘n’ roll, the band nods to the revolutionary unrest of author James Baldwin, the no-holds barred disillusionment of Ernest Hemingway, and Southern Gothic malaise of Flannery O’Connor.

In that respect, their sixth full-length and first of original material since 2013, Chains Are Broken [New West], resembles a dusty leather bound book of short stories from some bygone era.

“I always want our songs to unfold like short stories,” affirms Bernhard. “You could think of them like the chapters of a book. Of course, they’re shorter and maybe more poetic. This was a much more personal album about what it takes to be an artist or writer of any kind—and what you have to do to make your dream possible. It was really the headspace I was in. It might have something to do with getting older. You start reflecting on life and the people around you. I was doing that in these songs. That’s what makes the record more personal. I’m pulling from these things. Some of it is about drug addiction. Some of it is about the things you sacrifice. Some of it is about the detrimental things we do for inspiration. Nevertheless, they all have some sort of narrative.”

The Devil Makes Three’s journey up to this point could be deemed worthy o...

events.title: Jai Wolf
events.description:
After the success of indie-dance anthems like “Indian Summer” and “Starlight,” blockbuster festival sets from Indio to India, and co-signs from the likes of Skrillex and ODESZA, it’s clear from the opening notes of Jai Wolf’s long-awaited debut album The Cure to Loneliness that he sees the expectations around his name as an opportunity to challenge convention.

The Cure to Loneliness finds Jai Wolf completing his evolution from upstart bedroom remixer to future bass DJ to builder of lush musical worlds. While still very much dancefloor-focused, some tracks on the LP conjure the angular riffage of The Strokes and Phoenix, weave melodies through the sugary happysad of M83 and CHVRCHES, or build up walls of sound like Explosions in the Sky—all while maintaining the melodious polish and evocative groove to which fans have grown so close.

“In my heart, this album is me,” says Jai Wolf. “From the sounds to the lyrics, it’s everything that I’ve always wanted to do.” Taking a different approach to many of his contemporaries, Jai Wolf largely eschewed singles over the course of two years to patiently craft The Cure to Loneliness. The result is a thoughtfully framed, confidently expressed musical vision that will tug at heartstrings in 2019 and long beyond.

events.title: John Gorka
events.description:
Godfrey Daniels is one of the oldest and most venerable music institutions in eastern Pennsylvania. A small neighborhood coffeehouse and listening room, it has long been a hangout for music lovers and aspiring musicians, and, in the late 1970s, one of these was a young Moravian College student named John Gorka. Though his academic course work lay in Philosophy and History, music began to offer paramount enticements. Soon he found himself living in the club’s basement and acting as resident M.C. and soundman, encountering legendary folk troubadours like Canadian singer/songwriter Stan Rogers, Eric Andersen, Tom Paxton and Claudia Schmidt. Their brand of folk-inspired acoustic music inspired him, and before long he was performing his own songs - mostly as an opener for visiting acts. Soon he started traveling to New York City, where Jack Hardy’s legendary Fast Folk circle (a breeding ground for many a major singer/songwriter) became a powerful source of education and encouragement. Folk meccas like Texas’ Kerrville Folk Festival (where he won the New Folk Award in 1984) and Boston followed, and his stunningly soulful baritone voice and emerging songwriting began turning heads. Those who had at one time inspired him - Suzanne Vega, Bill Morrissey, Nanci Griffith, Christine Lavin, Shawn Colvin - had become his peers.

In 1987, the young Minnesota-based Red House Records caught wind of John’s talents and released his first album, I Know, to popular and critical acclaim. With unusu...

Now he’s back on the road with an hour of new material that puts everyone in the splash zone – politicians, celebrities, and pretty much anybody else who needs a comedy beatdown in what Failla refers to as “this funhouse we call America.” It’s a night of uncensored standup along with an audience Q&A that leaves nothing off limits, including, he claims, his famous Fox News friends.

events.title: Playing with Fire: An Ecosexual Emergency
events.description:
Beth Stephens & Annie Sprinkle IN PERSON!

Playing with Fire: An Ecosexual Emergency is a joyous ecosexual documentary born from the ashes of California’s devastating fires. When lightning ignites the redwood forest

surrounding their home in Boulder Creek, longtime lovers Beth Stephens and Annie Sprinkle are forced to evacuate — and their lives are forever transformed.

They blend loss and grief into ecosexual art, moving through fire as destructive, regenerative, and erotic forces, while fusing humor, community care, social justice and environmental

awareness into a lush and fiery journey of transformation.

The film unfolds through an ecosexual lens (imagining the Earth as a lover) while weaving stories from formerly incarcerated firefighters, an Indigenous scholar, fire artists, neighbors, a witch-therapist, a fire-play massage fetishist, and a fire tassel twirling burlesque queen.

Partially narrated by Boulder Creek’s mythical white peacock Albert and culminating in a ceremonial Wedding to Fire on a riverbank in the redwoods, Playing with Fire is a creative

and urgent call-to-action as the climate crisis worsens, and is a powerful portrait of queer resilience in the face of a world in flames.

Everclear, one of the leading alternative rock bands to emerge from the ‘90s, celebrated their 30th Anniversary in recent years, and founder, vocalist and guitarist Art Alexakis has made it clear that he has no plans to slow down. Since forming in 1992, Everclear has enjoyed a lengthy career by any measure, spanning 11 studio releases, including four that have been certified Gold or Platinum, selling over 6 million records, and achieving 12 Top 40 Hit Singles on Mainstream Rock, Alternative, and Adult Top 40 radio, including “Santa Monica,” “Father of Mine,” “I Will Buy You A New Life,” “Wonderful” and “Everything To Everyone,” as well as numerous videos, thousands of shows, and various other accolades, including a 1998 Grammy nomination.

After the demise of his band Colorfinger in 1992, Alexakis was struggling to make it in Portland, where he’d moved from San Francisco. In 2023, the band released its first new album in its best-selling series of tribute albums in 11 years. The series began with Dub Side Of The Moon (2003), the critically acclaimed reggae re-working of the classic Pink Floyd album, then continued with Radiodread (2006), Easy Star’s Lonely Hearts Dub Band (2009),and Easy Star’s Thrillah (2012), as well as the remix album Dubber Side of the Moon (2010). The All-Stars have also released two original collections, Until That Day EP (2008) and First Light (2011).

events.title: International Bottled Water Tasting Class
events.address: 57 Post Street, Suite 608, San Francisco, CA, 94104
events.description:
Think you can tell Fiji from Evian in a blind tasting? Know your Topo from your Pellegrino just from looking at the bubbles? Have you ever tried salty sparkling Spanish Vichy Catalan, or experienced the bizarre Borjomi from the Republic of Georgia?

Bottled waters differ dramatically in texture, minerality, carbonation, and finish. We’ll try lots of waters - some familiar and some super weird- and we’ll learn Why they taste the way they do in this alcohol-free experience.

We’ll start by blind tasting San Francisco tap to see if Hetch Hetchy is as heavenly as we’ve heard about. We’ll continue blind tasting bottled still waters from neutral to mineral-rich, then crack open a whole bunch of sparkling soda waters and go through them one-by-one.

events.title: One City One Book: Cities as Ancestors
events.description:
Explore how our relationships with cities, parks and the more-than-human world can shape our future. Inspired by Susanna Kwan's Awake in the Floating City, the 2026 One City One Book selection, this conversation brings together local community leaders working on place-based environmental justice to consider what it means to be an ancestor and how the places we inhabit become part of our collective legacy.

Drawing on five years of the Parks as Ancestors series, inspired by the book, What Kind of Ancestor Do You Want to Be?, the discussion expands the conversation beyond protected parklands to consider urban spaces as living legacies.

This interactive program invites participants to consider what we inherit from the places and people who came before us-and what we will leave behind for those who come after. Attendees are welcome to bring a photograph or a sentimental object honoring someone they have lost, if they wish to incorporate it into the program.

Free

Presented by San Francisco Public Library

events.description:
Identity and heritage converge as Chinese artists from around the world bring their stories to the screen.

China Moves presents dance films by filmmakers working inside China alongside those creating from afar. Eight films explore story, memory, and transformation across generations and geographies. Todas las reuniones son en español y se llevan a cabo en un ambiente positivo, familiar, y confidencial. Ven a compartir con nosotros, estamos seguros que encontrarás apoyo y recibirás información para mejorar tu calidad de vida.

SFAF ofrece servicios a cualquier persona sin importar su situación migratoria.

Para mas información sobre El Grupo, llama al 415-632-9722.

_____

Our support group, El Grupo, has been a stable source of family and community for Latinos, Latinas and their families since the early 1980s. Join us for information about sexual health and harm reduction, meals and social support, and help finding health and social services.

events.title: New People: The Great Experiment
events.description:
This screening will take place at NEW PEOPLE CINEMA, located at 1746 Post Street in Japantown.

Followed by a post-screening Q&A with Co-Director Eric Daniel Metzgar

THE GREAT EXPERIMENT is an epic poem in documentary form—a mirror held to an American nation at war with its own reflection, asking not who is right, but whether the experiment itself can survive.

Filmed in striking black and white across the US over four consequential years, from 2017 to 2021, the film considers the results of what George Washington once called “our last great experiment” in democracy.

The approach is spatial and observational—less interested in the ideological binary of left and right than in the vast, complicated country that exists at the intersection of many kinds of American experience.

Much as Robert Frank traveled the U.S. in the mid-1950s—bearing witness yet refusing to editorialize in his seminal photographic anthology of America—the film weaves these lives together not to resolve their contradictions, but to hold them in the same frame long enough for something surprising to emerge.

events.title: Maryna Krut
events.description:
Maryna Krut

Thursday, October 29 | The Freight

The Russian invasion of Ukraine transformed Maryna Krut from being a performer updating a beautiful tradition of music to being a witness testifying to people around the world about the devastating war in her homeland.

These days, the 30-year-old musician leads a double life. From her temporary home in the west of Ukraine, she travels to the front lines of the war to perform for soldiers. And she also travels abroad to perform, relating what she has seen—and thanking audiences for their support of the Ukrainian people.

Maryna plays the bandura, a Ukrainian string instrument that looks like a cross between a lute and a zither. Steeped as a child in her country’s traditional music, she now incorporates some non-traditional elements into her playing, principally jazz, using it both as a solo instrument and to accompany her powerful singing.

In Ukraine, she gained a national following after appearances on that country’s versions of “The X Factor” and “The Voice” as well as placing in Eurovision. Now she is expanding her audience as she brings the story andj culture of Ukraine to the world.

events.title: My Benjamin
events.description:
A visual essay on the loving acceptance of what comes to an end, starring Paris Opera Ballet Étoile Benjamin Pech.

My Benjamin follows Benjamin Pech during his final year as an Étoile at the Paris Opera Ballet, tracing the arc of his artistic life inside the storied Palais Garnier, from his entry into the Opera’s ballet school at age ten to the severe hip injury that now threatens to end his career.

Along the way, director Victoria Clay Mendoza and Pech develop an unexpected friendship in which each sees themselves reflected in the other: as Pech confronts a body that can no longer sustain him, Clay Mendoza faces her own return to Mexico to care for her mother, who has been diagnosed with Alzheimer’s.

A visual essay on endings, on the loving acceptance of deterioration, and on the need to be seen through these processes, My Benjamin renders the private world of ballet intimate and immediate, following Benjamin’s daily routine with rare access and tenderness.

Followed by a live Q&A with director Victoria Clay Mendoza, moderated by Sabrina Bot (MerciSF).

Luckily for Boyd, his mother’s familial wealth has given him the opportunity to be the first person in the history of the world to pilot an experimental technology: mechanical hands controlled entirely by his subconscious. Soon, however, the hands begin to move on their own… even when they’re not attached to Boyd’s body.

Chris Colfer playing Irish, Alice Krige playing a matriarch trying to rebuild her son at any cost. Add to the mix disembodied hands that come to life, a crumbling estate full of barbed arguments, and a gallery of characters as despicable as they are magnetic. events.description:
An intimate, unguarded look at the creative process of one of dance’s most singular voices: Emma Portner.

WORLD PREMIERE | Otter Lake follows choreographer Emma Portner as she turns to movement to reconnect with herself and confront her inner world. At just 31, Portner has become one of dance’s most distinctive voices, creating work for the National Ballet of Canada, the Norwegian National Ballet, and musical artists ranging from Justin Bieber to FKA Twigs.

This documentary offers a rare, intimate look inside her creative process, following Emma as she produces three new works, including pieces for the Royal Swedish Ballet and GöteborgsOperans Danskompani. Through a deeply personal lens, the film captures her vulnerability and brilliance alongside an unexpected bond formed during a transformative moment at her Otter Lake residence, offering a glimpse into the soul of an artist who communicates through movement when words fall short.

Followed by a live Q&A with Emma Portner and director Katya Mokolo.

events.title: Halloween (1978)
events.description:
In 1978, legendary New Yorker film critic Pauline Kael reviewed John Carpenter's HALLOWEEN. She didn’t like it.

"HALLOWEEN has a pitiful, amateurish script (by Carpenter and his producer, Debra Hill). An escaped lunatic wielding a kitchen knife stalks people in a small Midwestern town (Haddonfield, Illinois), and that's about it. Maybe when a horror film is stripped of everything but dumb scariness – when it isn't ashamed to revive the stalest device of the genre (the escaped lunatic) – it satisfies part of the audience in a more basic, childish way than sophisticated horror pictures do."

Eternal respect to Ms. Kael, but what she disdained more than 40 years ago are the very elements that have made this film endure for over four decades.

HALLOWEEN might not have resembled the “sophisticated” horror films of the 1970s, but the simplicity of the film’s story and production values allowed Carpenter to focus on staying one step ahead of the audience. From Dean Cundey's flowing, blue-hued photography to Carpenter's minimalist score to the blank, ominous mask of Michael Myers, nothing in this moody, terrifying film is misplaced.

Just as BLAZING SADDLES, DIE HARD, and THE MATRIX reinvigorated their genres by satisfying in “basic, childish ways,” Carpenter created a pitch-perfect prototype in HALLOWEEN that changed an entire genre forever.

Simon Posford is a pioneering force in psychedelic electronic music, shaping generations of artists through his groundbreaking work as Hallucinogen and SHPONGLE. In a place where girls and sport rarely mix, THE GYMNASTS OF FISHERMAN COLONY is a coming-of-age documentary where joy, ambition, and quiet rebellion take root as three teenage girls carve out space for themselves, one somersault at a time.

THE GYMNASTS OF FISHERMAN COLONY is an intimate coming-of-age documentary by 3X Emmy Award-winning filmmaker Habiba Nosheen that follows three teenage girls in Pakistan, offering a rare and tender portrait of girlhood, joy, and play told through the eyes of young Pakistani girls navigating the margins of society.

At its core, THE GYMNASTS OF FISHERMAN COLONY is a story of hope and quiet defiance. Through the intimate journeys of three teenagers we witness as their passion for gymnastics begins to clash with deeply rooted expectations around what girls can and cannot do. The film follows their journey as they find themselves straddling two polar opposite worlds as they push to make space for themselves through gymnastics. The result is a lyrical and deeply human portrait of three young girls from a corner of the world we rarely see on screen.

These are girls who dare to dream.

With soaring vocal harmonies and burning instrumental improvisation, framed by concise, poignant original songwriting, Wreckless Strangers seek to honor and carry forth the brand of free-spirited musical fun and adventure that defines the Bay Area.

The band features Amber Morris on lead vocals; David Noble on lead guitar and lead vocals; Joshua Zucker on bass and vocals; Mick Hellman on drums and vocals; Rob Anderson on guitar and vocals; and Fletcher Nielsen on keys.
Dirty Souls is the band’s third studio outing under the tutelage of Grammy-winning producer Dave Way, who fosters a level of depth and organic cohesion that firmly establishes Wreckless Strangers in San Francisco’s storied rock ’n’ roll legacy. Make Sunday, November 1, 2026, a night to remember at CrawlSF’s Dia De Los Muertos Pub Crawl—the spectacular closing chapter of the four-day Crawloween 2026 event.

Running from 4PM to 10PM, this uniquely themed pub crawl lets you continue the Halloween festivities while embracing the rich cultural traditions of Día de los Muertos.

Check in at the historic Mayes Oyster House (1233 Polk Street, San Francisco, CA 94109) and gain free access to participating bars including Mayes, McTeague’s, El Lopo, Wreck Room, Uni Pizza, Decodance, Lush Lounge, Beso Mae, and more. Throughout the evening you’ll find drink specials, DJs keeping the dance floors packed, free party favors, lively contests, and an atmosphere filled with celebration. Feel free to rock your best Halloween costume or dress in respectful Día de los Muertos style—traditional calavera face painting and attire are encouraged when worn to honor the holiday’s spirit of remembrance and joy.

events.title: The Musical Box
events.description:
Renowned for their high quality reproductions of historic Genesis performances since 1993, The Musical Box takes fans along for a time-travel ride, offering people a chance to relive the magic of this unique experience.

These replicas has required exhaustive visual, scenic, audio and musical research even tracking down the original music instruments used at the time. The visual aspect of The Musical Box shows are based on thousands of photos and many amateur films taken at the Genesis concerts, as well as the original slides used by the group during their shows.

Impressively, The Musical Box is the only group licensed and supported by Genesis and Peter Gabriel and has presented close to 1000 concerts across the world to more than one million spectators, in prestigious amphitheaters such as The Royal Albert Hall in London, the Olympia in Paris and the Bell Center in Montreal.

Peter Gabriel, who saw the concert was ”really impressed by the production quality and the attention to detail”; Steve Hackett and Phil Collins have even joined The Musical Box on stage.

''The Musical Box play it better than we did'' stated Phil Collins after seeing The Musical Box's production in Geneva.

A Musical Box show is a unique opportunity to discover the mystical Genesis concerts and to relive a historic rock moment.

events.title: Club Kid, in 35mm
events.description:
Another Planet Entertainment and SFFILM present
Club Kid (in 35mm)
Monday, November 2 | The Castro

Club Kid plunges audiences headfirst into the exhilarating, sybaritic universe of New York City nightlife. First-time writer-director Jordan Firstman stars as Peter, a magnetic club promoter whose lifestyle of revelry is upended when he unexpectedly discovers he fathered a young boy. Thrust into parenthood, Peter navigates his newfound responsibilities in fits and starts, relying heavily on his chosen family as he works to establish a philosophy for intimate love. Firstman’s script and performance deftly balance outrageous humor and anarchic energy with an unexpected emotional generosity. Newcomer Reggie Absolom is terrific as Peter’s son, Arlo, holding his own alongside a wonderfully unpredictable ensemble featuring Cara Delevingne, Diego Calva, Kirby Howell-Baptiste, Miss Benny, and Colleen Camp. Presented in 35mm, the film possesses a tactile physicality and vivid sense of place, while killer needle drops perfectly compliment the multitudes of Peter and Arlo’s experiences. Poignant and irreverent, Club Kid offers an insider’s glimpse into a distinctive culture while resonating with anyone who has struggled to find their place in the world. Funny, heartfelt, and singular, Club Kid is an irresistible invitation to experience something you won’t soon forget. —Jessie Fairbanks

events.title: Marjorie Keller: Intimate Observer
events.description:
Buy Tickets

Doors 6:30pm / Film 7pm

$15 / free or discounted for members

Marjorie Keller was one of the most significant figures in late 20th century American experimental film. A profoundly original artist, scholar, teacher and advocate, Keller was staunchly feminist without limiting herself to that movement’s ideological orthodoxies. Fiercely independent, her work was sharply critical of the customary role women were relegated to in patriarchal society, even as she embraced aspects of traditional family life. Keller cherished the mostly male history of avant-garde filmmaking, but she was one of the foremost advocates for women film artists throughout her life. When she died at age 43 in 1994, Keller had already produced twenty-seven 8mm and 16mm films. They were remarkable for their thematic and poetical complexity and by investigating her domestic life as a woman for their starting point. Her expressive cinematography and intricate montage were sensual, emotional and intellectually challenging, and while she was clearly influenced by such predecessors as Marie Menken, Stan Brakhage and Saul Levine, Keller's cinematic voice was distinctly her own from beginning with her first film.

In conjunction with the publication of a new book on Keller's work, In the Absence of Marjorie Keller, edited by Robin Blaetz and Scott Hammen, two programs of her films, spanning twenty-four years, will be presented by Berkeley Art Museum and Pacific Film Archive and San Francisco Cinematheq...
