Founded in 1977, Frameline is a San Francisco-based nonprofit media arts organization dedicated to the development, exhibition, distribution, and preservation of LGBTQ+ cinema and independent queer media.

Frameline Fall Showcase presents Elsinore

By 1989 acclaimed Scottish actor Ian Charleson (a sensational Andrew Scott, All of Us Strangers), who had career-defining roles in Oscar-winning pictures Chariots of Fire (1981) and Gandhi (1982), yearns for his next great role. For Charleson, a gay man with AIDS, navigating Hollywood and keeping his personal life private is a minefield, and he’s drawn to the idea of revisiting his stage-actor roots. When Daniel Day Lewis abandons Richard Eyre’s (Johnny Flynn, Ripley) production of Hamlet at the National Theatre mid-performance, Charleson is poised to take over the play’s title role.

But the actor’s ambitious return is halted when he develops Kaposi’s sarcoma, prompting his doctor (Oscar winner Olivia Colman, The Favourite) to forbid him from taking on such a strenuous role. Featuring memorable supporting turns from Joe Locke(Heartstopper) and David Dawson (My Policeman), who plays renowned queer filmmaker Derek Jarman, Simon Stone’s latest is a deeply resonant film about the power of art and human connection in the face of mortality, all moored by a career-best, Oscar-worthy performance from Scott.

events.description:
Solas is lighting up stages across the globe as they celebrate three decades of pushing boundaries and honoring traditions in Irish music. Hailed by The Boston Globe as “the finest Celtic ensemble this country has ever produced,” and by The Wall Street Journal as “an Irish traditional band bearing all the marks of greatness,” Solas continues to captivate audiences with their spellbinding musicianship and genre-defying creativity.

Formed in New York City in 1995, Solas quickly rose to prominence as a revolutionary force in Irish-American music. The very first iteration of Solas brought together a lineup of extraordinary talent including multi-instrumentalist Séamus Egan, fiddler Winifred Horan, vocalist Karan Casey, guitarist John Doyle, and accordionist John Williams. Together, they redefined the Celtic sound for a new generation, weaving traditional Irish tunes with elements of folk, bluegrass, Americana, and contemporary songwriting.

Now, with twelve critically acclaimed albums and a reputation for dynamic, emotionally charged live performances, Solas has set new standards for musicianship, repertoire, and intensity. Their debut album Solas (1996) established a bold new voice in traditional music, and each subsequent release has showcased the band’s remarkable ability to tell stories that resonate across time and cultures.

Among their most ambitious works is the 2013 concept album Shamrock City, a deeply personal project inspired by Egan’s great-great-uncle, who immigrat...

events.title: The Black Angels
events.description:
2026 marks the 20th anniversary of the band’s debut album, Passover (2006), a now-classic record that helped define the 21st-century psych revival. To celebrate, The Black Angels - Alex Maas (vocals/bass), Christian Bland (guitar), Stephanie Bailey (drums), Jake Garcia (guitar), and Misti Hamrick (bass) are returning to the road to perform the album in full, along with their greatest hits.

Formed in Austin, Texas in 2004, The Black Angels have become one of the most influential bands of the modern psychedelic rock movement. Drawing inspiration from forebears such as Syd Barrett, Roky Erickson, Arthur Lee, and The Velvet Underground, the band crafts a sound that is both reverent to the genre’s roots and fiercely forward-looking, hypnotic, heavy, political, and immersive.

Beyond their own recordings, the band’s impact on the global psychedelic community is cemented by their role as founders of Austin Psych Fest, one of the world’s most important gatherings for psychedelic, experimental, and underground music.

Following albums such as Death Song (2017) and Wilderness of Mirrors (2022) on Partisan Records, The Black Angels continue to evolve while remaining unmistakably themselves: a band that channels the spirit of classic psychedelia into a dark, modern, and deeply powerful form.

SYML is the solo venture of Seattle artist Brian Fennell. Welsh for “simple”— he makes music that taps into the instincts that drive us to places of sanctuary, whether that be a place or a person.

As an artist, Fennell takes license to both gut and be gutted. “If the dark inspires the good, that’s a good thing to be honest about,” he says.

events.title: Robert Shields: My Life as a Robot
events.description:
Robert Shields: My Life as a Robot celebrates the extraordinary, and often invisible, impact one artist can have on the world. In the 1970s, Robert Shields began performing his signature robot routine outside the Hollywood Wax Museum before later moving to street performances in San Francisco’s Union Square. Within a few short years, he and his wife, Lorene Yarnell, were headlining their own hit CBS variety series, The Shields & Yarnell Show. What Robert didn’t fully realize at the time was that his robot would go on to influence the DNA of popping, locking, and hip-hop dance as we know it today.

Funny, joyful, and full of genuine wonder, the film introduces you to a man who makes you believe anything is possible — including, as Robert demonstrates, street skiing through downtown San Francisco.

Followed by a live performance by Poppin John; a Q&A with Robert Shields, director Mark Bonn, producer Christine Seibert Bonn, and Poppin John, moderated by Peter L. Stein; and a post-screening reception in the lobby.

events.title: Two Films. One Manilatown Legacy.
events.description:
"Two Films. One Manilatown Legacy." brings two generations of San Francisco's Manilatown and International Hotel history to the big screen at SFMOMA for a special FREE double-feature presentation.

At 1 PM, experience the San Francisco premiere of the newly enhanced and restored edition of Curtis Choy's landmark 1983 documentary, "The Fall of the I-Hotel". The film chronicles the decade-long struggle to save San Francisco's International Hotel and the August 4, 1977 eviction of its predominantly Filipino and Chinese elder tenants. Following the screening, filmmaker Curtis Choy joins co-producers of the enhanced edition for a community conversation moderated by Caroline Ocampo.

At 3 PM, experience the premiere of "Manilatown Manang", the story of Jeanette Gandionco Lazam-artist, activist, and one of the few women who lived in the International Hotel as a Tenant Defender during the historic anti-eviction movement. The film follows Jeanette's journey from the I-Hotel struggle through a lifetime of activism, art, and community. Following the premiere, Jeanette Lazam joins the film's producers and creative team for a community conversation moderated by Caroline Ocampo.

Together, the films create a powerful dialogue between past and present: audiences first encounter Jeanette as a young activist in Choy's historic documentary, then experience the continuation of her story in Manilatown Manang.

events.title: Kolam: At the Threshold
events.address: 1700 Alum Rock Avenue, San Jose, CA, 95116
events.description:
Abhinaya Dance Company, an Indian classical dance company founded by Artistic Director Mythili Kumar announces Kolam: At the Threshold* on Saturday, November 7, 4 pm at the Mexican Heritage Plaza in San Jose.

Kolam: At the Threshold, choreographed by Abhinaya Principal Artist and Choreographer Rasika Kumar, is a new full-length 80-minute Bharatanatyam dance work that explores ritual, inheritance, and cultural memory through the South Indian practice of kolam-daily rice-flour drawings made at the threshold of the home. The piece integrates Bharatanatyam movement, Carnatic music, spoken text, and spatial design inspired by kolam's geometric structures.

Kolam centers the threshold as both a physical and symbolic space-between inside and outside, tradition and modernity, belonging and exclusion. The artistic vision is to transform the daily ritual of kolam into a contemporary performance structure, using its principles of symmetry, repetition, and impermanence as choreographic tools.

*Kolam: At the Threshold is inspired by the book Feeding a Thousand Souls: Women, Ritual, and Ecology in India- An Exploration of the Kolam, by Vijaya Nagarajan, Associate Professor in the Department of Theology and Religious Studies at the University of San Francisco.

$40-$70.

Presented by Abhinaya Dance Company

MARIANNE & LEONARD
WORDS OF LOVE

Sunday, November 8

Marianne & Leonard: Words of Love, renowned filmmaker Nick Broomfield’s documentary chronicles their relationship, from the early days in Greece. Conspiracy of Beards will sing a few songs before the movie starts!

The San Francisco Leonard Cohen Festival presents a screening of Marianne & Leonard: Words of Love, renowned filmmaker Nick Broomfield’s most personal and romantic film of his storied career. The documentary starts on the Greek island of Hydra in 1960, where Leonard Cohen, then a struggling and unknown fiction writer, and Marianne Ihlen, a single mother with a young son, became part of a community of expat artists, writers and musicians. Never-before-seen footage shot by Broomfield and legendary documentarian D.A. Pennebaker makes for a unique portrait of an idyllic 1960’s bohemia. It was a time that left a lasting imprint on both Marianne and Leonard, whose friendship would last another fifty years before their deaths in 2016.

Wajda’s first film where he received sole screenwriting credit, this deeply personal homage to his beloved actor Zbigniew Cybulski, the star of Ashes and Diamonds, is also a scathing portrait of the film industry.

The film-within-a-film mirrors the real life tragedy, with actors channeling their real life experiences into their performances. Weaving together autobiography and fiction, Wajda questions what it means to be an artist and how we mourn by creating legends as a way to interpret the past. A deeply personal homage that mirrors the tragic death of iconic actor Zbigniew Cybulski, the “Polish James Dean.”

Screenings of Andrzej Wajda’s films in the USA in 2026 are part of the ‘Wajda 100 Tour – North America’ project, organized by DI Factory with the financial support of the Polish Film Institute.

events.title: Jeffrey Foucault
events.description:
In two decades on the road Jeffrey Foucault has become one of the most distinctive voices in American music, refining a sound instantly recognizable for its simplicity and emotional power. With a string of critically acclaimed studio albums – “Stark, literate songs that are as wide open as the landscape of his native Midwest” (The New Yorker), "Beat-up troubadour folk whittled to dolorous perfection” (Uncut), “Songwriting Brilliance,” (Irish Times) – he’s built a brick-and-mortar international touring career and a devoted following, one that includes luminaries like Van Dyke Parks, Greil Marcus, and Don Henley.

In September of 2024 Jeffrey Foucault will release The Universal Fire (Fluff & Gravy, 9/6/24), his first album of entirely new material since 2018. A series of high-voltage performances cut live in one room, the album is both a working wake – Foucault lost his best friend and drummer Billy Conway, to cancer in 2021 – and a meditation on the nature of beauty, artifact, and loss.

Augmenting Foucault's all-star band with members of Calexico and Bon Iver (drummer John Convertino and producer/saxophonist Mike Lewis) The Universal Fire sets Conway’s death against the massive 2008 fire at the Universal Studios lot in California that destroyed the master recordings of some of our bedrock American music, to interrogate ideas about mortality, legacy, meaning, and calling.

events.title: Holy Wave
events.description:
In Ensenada, Mexico, where the Pacific horizon cuts a clean, unwavering line, Holy Wave recorded their latest full length, i’m DADA, a record that feels both expansive and newly concentrated for the subterranean pop four-piece. Stepping outside the United States was less a retreat than a shift in perspective, creating distance to recognize a new sound that had been slowly taking shape among them. i’m DADA quickly revealed its character: more propulsive, more candid, and their most structurally deliberate work to date.

Working alongside experimental duo Lorelle Meets the Obsolete at their studio El Derrumbe the sessions folded community into the album, though its emotional core had already formed over months of pre-production. Half of Holy Wave is Mexican, with roots in the El Paso border region, so recording in Ensenada felt intuitive and relaxed. Joo Joo Ashworth, mixing engineer and longtime friend, also provided a pivotal presence helping crystallize the album’s rhythmic language and subtly expanding the band’s sound. The songs began reflecting conversations about fatherhood and partnership, breakups and estrangement, the queasy acceleration of AI, and what it means to remain present and principled while the world lurches unpredictably forward.

Presented by Kilowatt.

events.description: Formed in 2000 on Long Island, New York, Brand New is an American alternative rock band consisting of Jesse Lacey, Vincent Accardi, Garrett Tierney, and Brian Lane. After signing with Triple Crown Records, the band released their debut album, Your Favorite Weapon, in 2001, establishing themselves within the Long Island emo and pop-punk scene. Their breakthrough second album, Deja Entendu, arrived in 2003 and featured the singles “The Quiet Things That No One Ever Knows” and “Sic Transit Gloria Glory Fades.” The album showcased a more mature sound and was later certified Gold in the United States. Following a major-label bidding war, the band signed with DreamWorks/Interscope and released The Devil and God Are Raging Inside Me in 2006, a record that would become one of the most influential albums of the emo era. In 2009, they put out their fourth album Daisy, reaching No. 6 on the Billboard 200. Brand New returned in 2017 with Science Fiction, which debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 and received widespread critical acclaim.

The project launched with "Te Juro Que No," with additional singles and collaborations arriving throughout 2026. This year also marked the band's acclaimed NPR Tiny Desk Concert, which received widespread praise from critics and fans alike, reaffirming Aterciopelados as one of Latin America's most compelling live acts.

El Grupo de Apoyo Latino de SFAF es un grupo social y educativo que ofrece un espacio abierto, seguro, y confidencial para apoyar a la comunidad Latina afectada por el VIH y SIDA. Es un grupo diverso, donde el respeto es la base para que todos los asistentes puedan expresar libremente sus experiencias, identidad, étnicidad, nacionalidad, sexualidad, y creencias religiosas.

Todas las reuniones son en español y se llevan a cabo en un ambiente positivo, familiar, y confidencial. Ven a compartir con nosotros, estamos seguros que encontrarás apoyo y recibirás información para mejorar tu calidad de vida.

SFAF ofrece servicios a cualquier persona sin importar su situación migratoria.

Para mas información sobre El Grupo, llama al 415-632-9722.

_____

Our support group, El Grupo, has been a stable source of family and community for Latinos, Latinas and their families since the early 1980s. Join us for information about sexual health and harm reduction, meals and social support, and help finding health and social services.

Meetings are in-person at 940 Howard St Group Room A every Thursday from 3 to 5 pm.

events.title: Ólafur Arnalds
events.description:
Another Planet Entertainment Presents
Ólafur Arnalds
Thursday, November 12 | The Castro

Award-winning artist, composer and producer Ólafur Arnalds returns with his most daring and adventurous project to date.

Falling Apart Together is an attempt at dismantling the distance between us. A concert hybrid that reveals the layers we construct in order to feel safe, the moments in which those layers tremble and the sense of intimacy and shared humanity that emerges when we allow ourselves to be exposed.

Together with his team of devoted craftsmen and musicians, Ólafur presents a spellbinding blend of past and new material in a show that challenges the boundaries of what a concert can be.

After his globally acclaimed tours following re:member and some kind of peace — which sold out such iconic halls as Royal Albert Hall, Elbphilharmonie, Sydney Opera House, and Walt Disney Concert Hall – performing to hundreds of thousands of fans worldwide — Ólafur returns with his most intimate and boundary-pushing work to date.

Falling Apart Together explores what becomes possible when we let ourselves unravel just enough to collectively open up.

events.description:

The Top Dawg Entertainment visionary returns with his third studio album on May 1, expanding his sonic world beyond hip-hop into cosmic jazz, psychedelic guitar rock, Soulquarian neo-soul, and flashes of genre-blurring experimentation. Since emerging from Chattanooga, TN in 2012, Rashad has built one of the most impactful and emotionally resonant catalogs in modern rap. His debut Cilvia Demo immediately established him as a critical force, followed by The Sun’s Tirade, which debuted in the Top 20 of the Billboard 200 and earned Gold certification. His 2021 album The House Is Burning further solidified his cultural imprint, amassing nearly one billion global streams and widespread acclaim for its introspective storytelling and sonic evolution. events.title: Cue the Music
events.description:
A music-driven night of rhythm, soul, and screen-shaking visuals at the SHACK15 social club.

Get ready for a high-energy evening where the music takes center stage. Cue the Music at SHACK15 transforms San Francisco’s iconic Ferry Building into a dynamic celebration of sound and movement on screen. This year’s soundtrack spans genres and generations: Grammy-winning artist Imogen Heap teams up with Pattie Gonia for a song about what we take for granted, global pop icon Harry Styles scores the unraveling of a relationship, and soul revivalists Durand Jones & The Indications set the tone for a night at the club gone thrillingly off-script. Blues powerhouse Susan Tedeschi and a mix of rising and independent artists round out a lineup built as much for the dance floor as the screen.

With the chance to mingle with festival filmmakers, this is more than a film screening — it’s a party for music lovers, dance fans, and anyone who wants to feel the beat in their feet.

Info and tickets: https://sfdancefilmfest.org/fall-festival-2026/cue-the-music/

events.title: Tuba Skinny
events.description:
Tuba Skinny

Thursday, November 12 | The Freight

For over a decade Tuba Skinny has grown steadily in popularity, releasing twelve albums and touring all over the world. They’ve attracted a wide variety of fans, young and old, neophytes and niche-enthusiasts, with the strength of their musicianship and the scope of their jazz and American roots music catalog. The band is composed of Shaye Cohn (cornet), Barnabus Jones (trombone), Todd Burdick (tuba), Craig Flory (clarinet), Gregory Sherman (guitar and vocals), Max Bien-Kahn (banjo), Robin Rapuzzi (washboard), and Erika Lewis (vocals and bass drum).

While they’ve become known as world-class interpreters of traditional jazz, over the years they’ve branched out into jug band music, spirituals, country blues, string band music, ragtime, and New Orleans R&B. Their approach is a true reflection of Americana, encompassing the full genealogy of popular American music from an early 20th century perspective.

No matter how well known they’ve become or how high profile their gigs have gotten, Tuba Skinny has always returned to the streets. “We continue to play in the street because it’s a public space,” says Shaye. “We get to play for everyone: old, young, rich, poor, people from all walks of life. It keeps things interesting because it’s organic and unpredictable.”

After a decade of playing (mostly) other artist’s songs, Tuba Skinny decided to fulfill a long-time dream with the release of Magnolia Stroll - their first album of all-or...

events.title: LIVE MUSIC: School Fair, goldenstar, Poor Image
events.description:
Throwin’ Bo’s presents:

School Fair

School Fair (Findlay Buchanan, Semisi Ma’ia’i, Hamish Morgan, De Stevens and Rose Pickernell) make music embedded in the human experience. It’s a product of the band’s native New Zealand, a place that remains intimate and remote, where emotion is magnified over both distance and familiarity. The five band members began the project renting out a factory-sized, sub-zero degree Celsius room normally operated by construction workers in the industrial area of Ōtepoti, Dunedin, New Zealand in 2021, recording music on the 4-track tape recorder that would become debut Gorse on a Hill. The album remained the only trace of the band online for a few years, an artifact for those who know where to look. School Fair’s music has this sense of self-discovery when you find it, a sound that feels both recognizable and like the vacant expanse of a country whirring by on a train. Still with little to no self-promotion, the appearance of sophomore effort Bird the Kid online in early 2025 was a new portal to their world of melodic and intricate indie music that retains a kind of atmospheric beauty.

Unexpected Violence (Mutual, 2026) is the first record made between geographical places, with the band now split in between London and New Zealand. You can hear this fragmented approach in the patchwork quality and inherent connective tissue of the album. events.description:

Weaving together chamber classical, folk, torch song, and experimental music, Dorian Wood’s Canto de Todes is a 70-minute distillation born from Wood’s acclaimed 12-hour composition and installation. The title—Spanish for “Song of Everyone”—is inspired by a lyric of the late Chilean singer and songwriter Violeta Parra. Canto de Todes emphasizes the urgency of music as a vessel for social change, and honors the ancestral trajectory of Wood’s Costa Rican-Nicaraguan family and their experience in the U.S.

Dorian Wood (b. 1975, pronouns: she/her/they/them) is an anti-disciplinary artist based in the U.S., whose practice seeks to “infect” spaces and ideologies in order to challenge traditions and systems of marginalization. Her performances, films and visual works have been presented worldwide. From 2019–2020, Wood toured internationally with XAVELA LUX AETERNA, a chamber orchestra tribute to Chavela Vargas. Subsequent works Mares Ocultos (2022), a compositional series centering on deconstructing male heterosexuality.

Born in San Juan, Puerto Rico, Roco Córdova is a vocalist, composer, producer and improviser based in the San Francisco Bay Area. They possess a B.Mus. in Composition from the Puerto Rico Conservatory of Music and an M.A. in Composition from Mills College in Oakland, California. San Francisco’s biggest South Asian celebration is back, and for the first time ever, it lands at Yerba Buena Gardens, one of downtown’s most iconic arts and cultural destinations.

On July 24 and November 13, Yerba Buena Gardens, Jessie Square, and Yerba Buena Lane will transform into a vibrant, open-air celebration of music, dance, food, and culture—bringing together community, creativity, and connection in the heart of downtown.

As the only outdoor celebration of its size and scale in the Bay Area dedicated to South Asian culture, Bhangra & Beats continues to create a space that is both rooted in tradition and alive with the energy of the Bay.

At the heart of it all is the vibrant Bhangra & Beats atmosphere, a family-friendly celebration where traditional Punjabi rhythms meet Bay Area energy. Non Stop Bhangra collective will once again lead the experience with its signature mix of interactive dance lessons, beautiful performances, live dhol drumming, DJs, and an open dance floor, all flowing into a lively marketplace with food vendors, local makers, community activations, restaurant and bar specials, and family-friendly activities.

Come for the music, stay for the energy. Whether you’re dancing, eating, shopping, or just taking it all in, there’s something here for everyone.

events.description:
Appearing on the rap scene in 1986 as Boogie Down Productions, releasing his first hit single “South Bronx” with his late DJ Scott La Rock, KRS “the one” made it clear that Hip Hop was going to have to take itself a lot more seriously than simply being a music genre.

KRS, an acronym for “Knowledge Reigning Supreme”, has been called the “conscience of Hip Hop” (Rolling Stone), “the greatest live emcee ever” (The Source), the “spokesperson for Hip Hop” (Wall Street Journal), “master teacher” (Zulu Nation) and the “son of Hip Hop” (Kool DJ Herc).

With 20 published albums to his credit and his numerous appearances with other artists, KRS-One is believed to have written the most rhymes in Hip Hop’s history. In the 1990s, as “hip-hop” grew more and more commercialized and corporate, it was KRS-One that openly rejected such cultural exploitation and materialism, grounding Hip Hop in its original principles of peace, love, unity, and safely having fun. Teaching everything from self-creation to stopping violence; from vegetarianism to transcendental meditation, from the establishment of Hip Hop Appreciation Week (every third week in May), to establishing Hip Hop as an international culture at the United Nations (2001), KRS-One has single-handedly held the history and original arts of Hip Hop together now for over two decades.

In addition to lecturing at over 500 universities in the United States and publishing three ground-breaking books; “The Science of Rap” (1995), “Ruminations”...

events.title: The Moth GrandSLAM Championship
events.description:
Another Planet Entertainment presents
The Moth GrandSLAM Championship

Friday, November 13 | The Castro

The Moth is dedicated to finding people from all walks of life to tell inspired stories. At The Moth StorySLAM, those people find us. On this night, winners from our StorySLAM series compete to determine The San Francisco GrandSLAM Story Champion.

The Moth GrandSLAM is the ultimate storytelling championship, inviting winners from The Moth’s open-mic StorySLAMs back to the stage to battle for the crown. With a full slate of local storytelling pros, you know this night is going to be good. Come experience fierce, hilarious, and sometimes even heartbreaking stories at the Moth GrandSLAM live.

The Moth is a global storytelling nonprofit with the mission to inspire people to listen and share openly, think and feel deeply, and expand their understanding of one another. Since 1997, The Moth has presented more than 70,000 true stories—told live and without notes—in 11 countries, across 4 continents. Today, The Moth produces 600+ live shows annually, as well as the Peabody Award-winning The Moth Radio Hour, and the popular The Moth Podcast. Through workshops for students, educators, adults, advocates, and professionals, The Moth guides thousands of new storytellers each year in finding and sharing their own voices. Learn more at themoth.org @MothStories

events.title: Jo Koy
events.description:
Jo Koy is one of today’s premier stand-up comedians, rising from performing in a Las Vegas coffee house to selling out arenas worldwide. His relatable comedy, drawn from his colorful family and Filipino heritage, has connected with audiences across cultures, making him one of the top 10 grossing stand-up comedians each year according to Pollstar and Billboard. He continues selling out and breaking records at prestigious venues around the world.

In 2023, Koy inked a two-special deal with Netflix, with the first special released in 2024. Jo Koy: Live From Brooklyn, filmed at the historic King’s Theatre, premiered globally on June 4 and was the #6 most viewed special that year, with over 240 million minutes watched. He recently filmed his upcoming Netflix special in Stockton, CA, set to release later this year. His other Netflix specials include Live From The Los Angeles Forum, Comin’ In Hot, and Live From Seattle. He also released the variety special Jo Koy: In His Elements, spotlighting Filipino-American culture in Manila. Overall, Koy has had seven highly rated specials across Comedy Central and Netflix.

Koy starred in the 2022 Universal Pictures comedy Easter Sunday, inspired by his life and Filipino roots, produced by Steven Spielberg’s Amblin Partners. He has also appeared in Disney’s Haunted Mansion, voiced characters in Netflix’s Monkey King and Leo, and most recently in Paramount+’s The Tiger’s Apprentice. On television, he has appeared in Mr. Iglesias and Comedy Cent...

events.title: Kino
events.description: Born in the underground clubs of Leningrad in 1981, KINO became the defining voice of Soviet rock — a band that smuggled freedom into every chord when freedom itself was contraband. Fronted by the magnetic Viktor Tsoi, they played to 62,000 at Moscow's Luzhniki Stadium in 1990. Months later, Tsoi was gone. The music never stopped. "What Elvis Presley was to America, Tsoi was to Russia." Now, original members Yuri Kasparyan, Alexander Titov, and Igor Tikhomirov bring KINO back to the stage — accompanied by Tsoi's own voice, restored and digitized from original multi-track recordings. This is not a tribute act. This is KINO, continuing the conversation. Expect anthems you know by heart — Gruppa Krovi, Peremen, Posledniy Geroy — performed with the raw urgency that made them timeless. Sung in Russian. Felt in every language.

events.title: Max Jaffe: You Want That Too! + Burden of Dreams
events.description:
Buy Tickets

Doors 8pm / Show 8:30pm

$23 / free or discounted for members

In a trio formation with some of the core rhythm section players from the record, Max Jaffe, Gavin Gamboa, and Logan Kane reimagine the music from Jaffe's 2025 release You Want That Too!

Max Jaffe is a drummer, producer, composer, and technologist based in Los Angeles, CA. His work expands the possibilities of composition and collaboration through the drum set.

In 2025, Jaffe released "You Want That Too!" on Colorfield Records. Eclectic and tuneful, the album received praise from Pitchfork and is being followed with a series of special live performances in varying formations.

Max is a founding member of experimental rock collective JOBS, Amirtha Kidambi's Elder Ones, and several others. He has toured, performed, and recorded with many diverse artists including Wild Up, Steph Richards, Nels Cline, Ava Mendoza, Cass McCombs, DARKSIDE, Normal Love, Jeff Parker, Vinny Golia, Peter Evans, and many others.

Burden of Dreams is the latest band from Oakland composer and multi-instrumentalist, Nathan Clevenger. Along with Clevenger on electric bass, the ensemble features Brett Carson (Hammond organ), Mark Pascucci-Clifford (vibraphone), and Jason Levis (drums). The band's music is dark and dense, drawing from 20th Century classical, doom rock, and jazz.

Photo by Alex De La Hidalga.

events.description:
This is Your City. This is Your Voice. This is Your Future. Share your story about growing up and raising your family in San Francisco.

Every family has a story. Every voice matters. Please share yours.

Join us for the District 4 Sunset Family Summit! The This Is Your City: Family Summit Series invites families, caregivers, young people, and community members from across San Francisco to help shape the future of our city.

Saturday, Nov. 14, 2026, 11:00 a.m. - 1:30 p.m.

Sunset Recreation Center, 2201 Lawton St, SF, CA 94122

Free food, childcare, and interpretation are provided. Please note all interpretation requests must be made 48 hours or more prior to the Family Summit.

Who should attend? Everyone is welcome. This event highlights District 4, but you can attend any Family Summit that fits your schedule.

Why are we gathering? The Family Summit Series is part of San Francisco's first Citywide Community Needs Assessment. Through conversations with families across the city, we're learning what matters most to children, youth, young adults, and families. What we learn will help improve future planning, programs, and services.

Whether you've lived in San Francisco your whole life or recently made it your home, your experiences and ideas matter.

Another Planet Entertainment Presents
Bonobo

Saturday, November 14 | Fox Theater

“Oh yeah, I guess I did do some of that stuff,” says Simon Green, as he reflects on his 25-year-plus career as the man behind the music of Bonobo. It’s a typically self-effacing response from an artist who has spent that time forging a path as one of the defining voices in electronic music. A path that along the way has seen him release two Top-10 Albums (2017’s ‘Migration’ and 2022’s ‘Fragments, which both landed at #5 on the UK chart), plus numerous Gold and Silver certified singles, sell over 900,000 records, rack up billions of streams, collaborate with the likes of Erykah Badu and Damon Albarn, and be both BRIT and GRAMMY-nominated – the latter seven times, with five in the dance/electronic categories, a record number of nominations shared with The Chemical Brothers, Skrillex and Madonna.

His renowned live show – built around a full live-band, guest vocalists and immersive visuals – has also set the blueprint for how and where an electronic musician can translate their records into the live arena. He has performed to millions of people across the globe, with sold-out shows at prestigious venues like the Sydney Opera House, Alexandra Palace and Red Rocks Amphitheatre – in many cases as one of the first electronic artists to do so – and the world’s biggest festival stages including Glastonbury, Coachella, Sonar and Fuji Rock. His last tour also included both a co-headline of London’s Field...

events.title: Paul Cauthen
events.description:
Another Planet Entertainment presents
The Book of Paul Tour
Paul Cauthen
Saturday, November 14 | The Castro

Whether he knows it or not, every man lives by a code. And for country provocateur Paul Cauthen, that code is simple. Always bet on yourself. A singer-songwriter with a well-documented distaste for playing by anyone else’s rules, the East Texas native spent two decades clawing his way through the country underground, embodying the independent spirit with a monolithic Big Velvet vocal. Fusing classic-country grit, gospel power, and a rhinestoned rock edge, four previous albums proclaimed his singular style with a booming baritone and near-biblical swagger. Taught to sing by his grandfather in a Church of Christ, Cauthen hit the scene with the duo Sons of Fathers in 2009, before My Gospel, Room 41, Country Coming Down, and Black on Black unveiled a vulnerable, fire-and-brimstone songwriter with brazen Texas attitude – craving deliverance, yet possessed by a “bird dog” instinct for theatrical rapture. Cauthen has toured the world, collaborating with Margo Price, Orville Peck, Cody Jinks, and Lana Del Rey. And with favorites like “Cocaine Country Dancing,” “Fuck You Money,” and his GOLD-certified collab with Shaboozey on “Last Of My Kind,” he counts 442 million global streams. Cauthen’s fifth album, Book of Paul, takes him further down his path of utterly authentic country music; fearless, proud, and with two middle fingers in the air. Co-writing 12 of 13 tracks, the troub...

Rexx Life Raj has spent ten years proving an artist can build it all on his own terms: the catalog, the audience, the story. From Berkeley, without a major label, he has built a catalog with more than 500 million streams, headlined tours nationwide, and developed one of the most engaged direct-to-fan communities in independent music.

That independence forced him to become more than a recording artist. Raj learned advertising, production, video, audience strategy, and creative technology firsthand, and now applies them across everything he touches, from fan experiences to app building to brand collaborations he treats as creative partnerships rather than endorsements.

His collaborators include Kehlani, E-40, Russ, Kenny Beats, and Larry June. His model is his own. For artists trying to build sustainable careers without giving themselves away, Raj is what the finished blueprint looks like.

events.title: Headache
events.description:
Thank You For Almost Everything is the sophomore album for Headache, a collaboration between writer and poet Francis Hornsby Clark and music-producer Joseph Thornalley aka Vegyn. This new album follows on the surprise underground success of their debut: The Head Hurts But The Heart Knows The Truth (released 31 May 2023) releasing on Vegyn’s own PLZ Make It Ruins label.

The debut record has streamed over 19.4 million times on Spotify alone and sold over 8,000 physical copies worldwide. The debut gained its popularity entirely organically with zero marketing or PR spend. Since its release, Headache has built a dedicated global fanbase, with several fans even going so far as to get lyrics or the project’s logo tattooed on themselves.

Thank You For Almost Everything continues the original’s distinct style of Trip-Hop / Downtempo Electronica but combining with its own unique (and now imitated) AI-voiced spoken word. For this new album, Headache steps away from the hum-drum of Blighty and instead focuses his gaze to sunnier shores. Recalling personal histories of ruffled hair and school cafeterias, ancient unsolved Albionic riddles, Rome’s changing seasons and its poignant graffiti, arguments with girlfriends at luxury hotel beachfront restaurants, and what it truly feels like to be alive in this inscrutable but beautiful world.

The project features a further collaboration with artist Cali Thornhill DeWitt who returns to design the packaging and cover for this new album. This do...

A mosaic of emotive piano keys, physical percussion, buzzing analog synths, and expansive vocals, RHYE find humanity in musicality. Shrouded in mystery, the group first surfaced setting the Internet abuzz with ambiguous imagery, sophisticatedly sensual music videos, and that distinctive falsetto. Following the runaway online success of two initial singles, the critically acclaimed debut album Woman (Loma Vista Recordings) was released in 2013 and lauded by critics from Pitchfork ("Best New Album") to The Guardian to New York Times.

Gifted songwriting, breathtaking vocals and deft instrumental arrangements combine to create an intoxicating blend of R&B influenced, deeply emotive music making the album a staple for provoking intimate moments.

Since the release of Woman, RHYE has relentlessly toured to establish a devoted global fanbase and enrapture crowds in theaters and at festivals worldwide including riveting sets at Coachella and Pitchfork Paris amongst many others.

Originally a duo conceived in the studio, RHYE has transformed into a collective led by vocalist and producer Milosh and elevated by a cast of accomplished multi-instrumentalists. As the band began writing new material, the expansive live show...

events.title: Paranda Party 3: Jeeti Raho
events.description:
Paranda Party is a queer South Asian cultural celebration built around the paranda, a punjabi hair tassel that is braided into the hair. Now in its third year, this is a night where South Asian culture and queerness share the same room.

This year's theme, Jeeti Raho, takes its name from the blessings our elders give us: jeeti raho, khush raho, abad raho. Stay living, stay happy, stay prosperous. Many of us grew up hearing body-shaming comments in the place those blessings should have been. Jeeti Raho reclaims them, on our own terms.

Join us November 7, 2026 at Queer Arts Featured in the Castro for an evening of live performance, original poetry, and paranda tradition brought to life. Expect original music and spoken word from South Asian and queer artists, a close look at the craft of paranda-making, and a collaborative zine filled with community poetry and artwork, available to take home.

Whether you're returning for your third Paranda Party or walking in for the first time, come ready to celebrate, be loud, and be fully yourself.

The story of a racing car driver who undergoes so many transplants that it can no longer be determined which people have contributed to his make-up.

Rally driver Richard Fox keeps getting involved in terrible accidents but always manages to survive thanks to organs transplanted from people who died in crashes he caused. The situation complicates when he starts acquiring his donors’ personality traits along with their organs.

Hunting Flies – Runtime: 104 minutes

Wlodek is a shy man who’s afraid of his mother as well as his wife. However, upon meeting Irena, his life takes a new turn.

One of the key films of the Polish film renaissance, this satiric comedy explores the seeming world of emancipated women and emasculated men in Communist Poland. A librarian shares his life and home with his domineering wife. He has an affair with a beautiful intellectual, who wears fly-shaped glasses. She tries to become the woman behind the great artist. It’s a film dedicated to the women of Poland, even as it critiques the relations between the sexes.

Screenings of Andrzej Wajda’s films in the USA in 2026 are part of the ‘Wajda 100 Tour – North America’ project, organized by DI Factory with the financial support of the Polish Film Institute.

events.description:
Goldenvoice Presents
Cry Baby Tour
Vince Staples
Sunday, November 15 | The Warfield

It opens with the ephemeral sounds of nature. Birds, bugs, and airy notes chiming in the air. Then, the undercurrent of something darker, disrupting the fantasy: a distorted voice. “To live is to be,” the voice says, “Like the nigga in the tree.” This is how Dark Times, Vince Staples’ eighth studio album, begins.

It’s a new era in the prolific artist’s canon, a muscular and revelatory work refining elements that have been present in his catalog for the last decade: dense lyricism over lush, layered beats; wry, melancholic observations about life; finding pockets of light in an endless dark. For Staples, the album is “a snapshot” of this period of his life.

“It’s been 10 years since I started putting things out properly,” he says, referencing his first EP, with Def Jam in 2014, Shyne Coldchain Vol 2, “I don’t really keep track of any of that stuff, but it’s important to take a second to appreciate the journey.” The title came intuitively to Staples after he listened to the record in full, noticing heavy motifs that kept reappearing. The album cover, featuring a faintly seen noose, was similarly intuitive.

We live in a time when our thumbs know more than our minds. We scroll past each other’s joy and grief before breakfast, absorb a day’s worth of tragedy by lunch, and still convince ourselves that the next notification might be the dopamine hit that’ll make us feel better. As much as some of us complain about smartphones — or, more specifically, what’s on said smartphones — distraction is the air we breathe. Social media, surveillance, endless updates and countless opinions, it all piles up until focus feels like a luxury item. For Thundercat, the clutter isn’t abstract. And on Distracted, his long-awaited fifth studio album, it’s the central theme of his life and art right now.

“If you got an Instagram, you know exactly what I’m talking about,” he says matter-of-factly, half joking, half exhausted, when asked the impetus of the album’s title. Thundercat doesn’t frame distraction as a buzzword or a diagnosis; instead, he treats it like something omnipresent, something you deal with whether you like it or not. Distracted arrives six years after 2020’s It Is What It Is, an album shaped by grief, romantic heartbreak, and the sudden loss of his friend and collaborator Mac Miller. If that record felt like a long exhale after trauma, Distracted feels like the restless pacing that follows: the period when life keeps happening whether you’re ready or not. It’s laughing through the pain, using humor as an aid to deal with the BS.

events.title: Hamilton Leithauser + Rostam
events.description:
Another Planet Entertainment presents
The Joint Tour
Hamilton Leithauser + Rostam
Wednesday, November 18 | The Castro

At the time I Had a Dream That You Were Mine was first released, the Hamilton Leithauser and Rostam were best known for their work in two of the most influential rock bands of the era: Hamilton as lead singer in The Walkmen and Rostam as the co-songwriter and producer behind Vampire Weekend. The inspired collaboration was born of friendship, and mutual admiration, but grew into a synergistic creative partnership that birthed a timeless album of beautifully evocative songs. I Had a Dream That You Were Mine is a delightfully immersive album, built around Rostam’s meticulous, expansive production and Hamilton’s distinctive, wild vocal range. Unlike anything either artist had done before, the album’s stylistic flourishes include doo-wop, country-rock, baroque pop, folk, and spellbinding torch songs. Together, the lauded musicians found a unique flair for the dramatic which made their handful of live performances a thrilling experience; ten years on, these rare live shows are not to be missed!

events.title: Kabaka Pyramid
events.description:
Kabaka Pyramid is a Grammy Award Winning Rastafarian lyricist fusing elements of Reggae, Hip Hop and Dancehall to create a unique sound, revolutionizing Jamaican music with conscious messages.

A key pillar of the Reggae Revival movement, Kabaka Pyramid carved his way into the Jamaican reggae scene with Rebel Music in 2011 with marquee songs like ‘Free From Chains’ and ‘Warrior’ featuring Protoje. His hip hop roots were evident in the lyrical style and hard-hitting beats, laying the foundation for an ever-ascending career highlighted by the Grammy winning album “The Kalling” produced by role model Damian Marley.

The Kingston native, born Keron Salmon, spent many of his early years developing his sound as a part of Bebble Team, a talented group of friends and schoolmates that would be the foundation of his independent label Bebble Rock. ‘Rebel Music’ was the fruit of this preparation and Kabaka’s career as a reggae artist was born. After touring Europe in 2012, prominent producers would take an interest, and hit songs ‘Mi Alright’ featuring Chronixx and ‘Well Done’ produced by Damian Marley would follow in 2013 and 2014 respectively. The ‘Accurate’ mixtape by Major Lazer’s Walshy Fire would see Kabaka collaborate with Raekwon on Be Inspired, and classic ‘Kabaka vs Pyramid’ would become a staple for true Kabaka fans.

Icona Pop always represented the ultimate freedom of expression for its two members and longtime friends: Caroline Hjelt and Aino Jawo. Their freedom as women and artists has underscored their thriving impact and influence as one of pop music’s most innovative and irresistible multiplatinum chart-topping forces. However, their third full-length album, Ritual, is actually about ownership. They are owning who they are as mothers, creative partners, entrepreneurs, leaders, sisters, and women. These women are running the dancefloor now. Caroline and Aino went from being club kids in Stockholm to commanding clubs, arenas, and festivals from the stage. Following an independent grind, Icona Pop first reached critical mass during 2012. The duo’s breakout single, “I Love It” [feat. Charli XCX], has endured as a generational banger. It went RIAA 5x-Platinum, sold north of 10 million digital singles, and even entered rarified air as part of Spotify’s “Billions Club” with over 1.2 billion streams on the platform. Following their Gold-certified full-length debut, This Is… Icona Pop in 2013, they notched two more Gold singles, headlined sold out tours, and supported the likes of Miley Cyrus, One Direction, The Chainsmokers, and the late Avicii. events.description:
Throwin’ Bo’s presents:

Babehoven

Babehoven is the Hudson, NY based project of singer-songwriter Maya Bon and collaborator Ryan Albert. Since 2017, the band has carved out a sound that blends melodic indie and folk rock with an occasional nod towards country. Bon serves as the project’s principal songwriter and lyricist, while Albert, a multi-instrumentalist and producer, further shapes the sonic world around her songs. Together, they’ve built a body of work that feels both intimate and expansive.

"Blue Around You," Babehoven's new single, is a country-flecked stomper. The song finds Bon singing with hard-won resilience: "Yesterday a stranger told me they can see / That I feel levels of pain that could've broken me / And I thought, mmm but I survived it." Recorded at The Chicken Shack and 12 Lb Genius in Upstate NY, Maya and Ryan gathered an excellent crew of musicians with producer Phil Weinrobe at the helm—Oliver Hill, Zosha Warpeha, Dylan Nowik, Jared Samuel, Ellington Peet, and Nick Kinsey. The core of the song was recorded live with no playback or headphones with the feel of the room being as much an instrument as the hardanger fiddle and harmonies that soar overhead.

events.title: Ann M. Evans and Georgeanne Brennan, Market Memories Cookbook
events.description:
Saturday, November 21, 2026, 11:00 am - 11:45 am

Stop by the Foodwise Classroom for a cooking demo featuring the seasonal bounty of the Ferry Plaza Farmers Market.

Georgeanne Brennan is a James Beard and Julia Child award-winning cookbook author. Her association with farmers markets goes back to the 1980s, when her pioneering seed company, Le Marche Seeds, supplied emerging market growers across the country. Her memoir, A Pig in Provence, chronicles her adventures in France, where she still has a home, raising pigs and making goats milk cheese. She lives in Winters, California, with her husband.

Ann M. Evans is a co-founder of the Davis Farmers Market and the Davis Food Co-op, and she is a former mayor of Davis, California. A leading proponent of the Farm-to-School movement in California, she worked extensively with former California School Superintendent Delaine Eastin and with Alice Waters on multiple projects. She writes a weekly column for the Davis Enterprise. This is her third cookbook. She lives with her husband in Davis.

They are the co-authors of Market Memories Cookbook: Celebrating 50 Years.

All demos take place in the Foodwise Classroom (green tent in front of the Ferry Building) and are free to the public, with recipes and samples for all.

The demo will be followed by a book signing with book sales courtesy of Book Passage.

events.description:
Think you can tell Fiji from Evian in a blind tasting? Know your Topo from your Pellegrino just from looking at the bubbles? Have you ever tried salty sparkling Spanish Vichy Catalan, or experienced the bizarre Borjomi from the Republic of Georgia?

Bottled waters differ dramatically in texture, minerality, carbonation, and finish. We’ll try lots of waters - some familiar and some super weird- and we’ll learn Why they taste the way they do in this alcohol-free experience.

We’ll start by blind tasting San Francisco tap to see if Hetch Hetchy is as heavenly as we’ve heard about. We’ll continue blind tasting bottled still waters from neutral to mineral-rich, then crack open a whole bunch of sparkling soda waters and go through them one-by-one.

events.description:
LOCATION

4127 18th Street

San Francisco, CA 94114

ADMISSION

$35; Museum admission included in tour

RSVP and reserve tickets here

The GLBT Historical Society Museum is pleased to partner with Unspeakable Vice to offer a monthly walking tour focused on the history of LGBTQIA+ resistance in the Castro neighborhood. Created by tour guide, former senior adjunct professor, and practicing designer Shawn Sprockett, Unspeakable Vice began as a close look at the queer origins of San Francisco, traversing the city’s North Beach and Barbary Coast areas to trace the history through from 1770-1960. This new tour closes a three-part story, extending Sprockett’s detailed and engaging storytelling to the Castro neighborhood.

Ten years after the White Night riots, the police came back. Meet the trans man doctors turned away, the lesbians who ran the blood drives and wards, and the community that answered a plague and two police riots with the same refusal. This tour includes a free round at the Lookout, overlooking the neighborhood you've just walked.

Details

Duration: about 90 minutes, plus the round afterward

Meet: GLBT Historical Society, 4127 18th Street

Ends: the Lookout, 3600 16th St at Market

Terrain: city sidewalks with one moderate hill; the Lookout is upstairs, stairs only

Ages: 21+ (free round, one per guest)

Heavy Rain: tours reschedule; your ticket transfers

events.title: Lucy Kaplansky
events.description:
She started out singing in Chicago folk music clubs as a teenager. Then, barely out of high school, Lucy Kaplansky took off for New York City. There she found a fertile community of songwriters and performers—Suzanne Vega, Steve Forbert, The Roches, and others. With a beautiful flair for harmony, Lucy was everyone’s favorite singing partner, but most often she found herself singing as a duo with Shawn Colvin. People envisioned big things for them; in fact, The New York Times said it was “easy to predict stardom for her.” But then Lucy dropped it all.

Convinced that her calling was in another direction, Lucy left the musical fast track to pursue a doctorate in clinical psychology. Upon completing her degree, Dr. Kaplansky took a job at a New York hospital working with chronically mentally ill adults, and also started a private practice. Yet she continued to sing. Lucy was often pulled back into the studio by her friends, (who now had contracts with record labels) wanting her to sing on their albums. She harmonized on Colvin’s Grammy-winning "Steady On," and on Nanci Griffith’s "Lone Star State of Mind" and "Little Love Affairs." She also landed soundtrack credits, singing with Suzanne Vega on "Pretty in Pink" and with Griffith on "The Firm," and several commercial credits as well—including “The Heartbeat of America” for Chevrolet.

Then Shawn Colvin—who was itching to produce a record—hooked up with Lucy, her ex-singing partner. They went into the studio, and when Lucy’s solo...

events.title: Pearl
events.description:
The allure of stardom on the big screen proves to be a road to some very dark places for Mia Goth’s titular PEARL in this stylish and gruesome prequel to Ti West’s X. With her husband away at war, Pearl finds herself dreaming of a way to escape from her boring life on the farm. She sees the silver screen as her way to find stardom and the love she so desperately needs, but her overbearing mother and her own dark impulses might hold her back from the fame she craves.

PEARL proves to be a delightfully perverse study on a standout character from writer/director Ti West’s tribute to ‘70s grindhouse, X. Its vibrant, candy-coated veneer plays wonderfully against the depraved desires of the main character bubbling just below the surface. Co-writer/star Mia Goth gives another deliciously unhinged performance as Pearl, a not-quite-innocent farm girl looking for love in all the wrong places. As much a love letter to the Golden Age of Hollywood as it is a demented look at the darkness bubbling just below the surface of rural America, PEARL is colorful, unnerving, and twisted in all the right ways.

events.title: Gary Numan
events.description:
In a castle in the San Fernando Valley lies the lair of music icon Gary Numan. Outside is an enormous statue of a dragon, inside a St Bernard (almost as large) greets you on arrival. He's a new addition to the family – a rescue pup, and huge. The lord of this manor could be as outwardly intimidating as this entire set-up, but he's a humble presence. Notorious for hits such as 'Are 'Friends' Electric?' and 'Cars', Numan's early career was too often misconstrued, tainted by a sometimes fraught relationship with the media and challenged by the hostility of the music industry at the time, still deeply committed as it was to the guitar, bass, drums approach of old. Numan, however, stuck to his guns, outlasted his naysayers, and became renowned not just as a pioneer but as an institution. Today, with a career that has spanned nearly four decades, his approach to electronic music remains an inspiration to artists across genres and eras, from stadium goliaths such as Depeche Mode, Prince and Nine Inch Nails to alternative heroes such as Beck, Damon Albarn and Marilyn Manson. Even Kanye West owes him a debt and David Bowie once credited him with ‘writing two of the finest songs’ in British music. It's no surprise he recently received the Ivor Novello Award for Inspiration.

Now, Numan is preparing his 22nd studio album titled ' Savage (Songs From A Broken World)'. He's a busy guy. A self-proclaimed “one man band”, Numan has always been something of an outlier living on his own terms....

events.title: Song Dongye
events.description: On June 29, 2026, Beijing singer-songwriter Song Dongye released Take Another Moment, his second album and his first full-length release in thirteen years. On this world tour, the new songs will be presented alongside the old favorites that have stayed with listeners all these years. Between 2017 and 2018, Song Dongye released three pivotal singles—“Empty Harbor Song,” “Guo Yuan Chao,” and “To Know”—each quietly expanding the boundaries of folk music and reshaping the industry’s perception of him. Now, thirteen years after his landmark debut Anhe Bridge North, arrives his long-awaited second album, Take Another Moment. Entirely self-conceived, arranged, and produced, it stands as a work that, even now, surpasses all expectations upon listening. Over the years, he has lost weight. He fishes. He takes photographs. He plays with beads. And he has completed Take Another Moment, an album astonishing in both its lyrical scope and sonic depth. He remains the songwriter, arranger, and producer at the center of his work. Alongside him are more than twenty instruments and sound sources, leading lights of China’s jazz world such as Wen Zhiyong, Xia Jia, and Nathaniel Gao, and independent spirits as subtle and reclusive as Xing Jiangbo He is still occasionally playful, perhaps as a way of balancing his absolute seriousness and devotion to music—once even letting his cat's backside appear on an album cover. events.description:
Another Planet Entertainment presents
The Music of Hey Arnold Live! Featuring Jim Lang & the PS 118 AllStars
with special guest Craig Bartlett

Tuesday, November 24 | The Castro

The Music of Hey Arnold! Live featuring Jim Lang & The PS 118 AllStars celebrates the 30th anniversary of one of television’s most cherished animated series.

Led by award winning composer Jim Lang, best known for his unforgettable theme music, original songs, and score for Hey Arnold!, this one of a kind concert brings the music of the series to life on stage. Blending jazz, hip hop, blues, R&B and funk, Lang created a sound unlike anything else on television, helping give Hey Arnold! its heart, warmth, humor and soul. Thirty years later, the music continues to connect with fans of all ages and inspire musicians around the world.

Performed by Jim Lang and The PS 118 AllStars, the evening features the show’s unforgettable themes, fan favorite songs, and some of the moments that made Hey Arnold! so special. Accompanied by multimedia visuals and stories from behind the music, the performance also includes a special guest appearance by series creator Craig Bartlett.

Whether you grew up with Hey Arnold! or are discovering its music for the first time, this 30th anniversary celebration is a chance to experience one of animation’s most distinctive and enduring scores performed live by the composer who created it.

events.title: The Wrecks
events.description:
The Wrecks are nothing if not resourceful.

The group’s very origin story is a testament to a rare level of D.I.Y. craftiness that has quietly cemented them as an independent phenomenon with an intensely faithful fan base, over a quarter-of-a-billion streams, and successive sold-out headline tours.

Rewinding back to the beginning, the Los Angeles-based band— Nick Anderson [vocals, guitar, keyboard, production], Nicholas “Schmizz” Schmidt [lead guitar], Aaron Kelley [bass], and William “Billy” Nally [drums]—actually recorded their first batch of tunes under clandestine cover in a “borrowed studio.”

Leaving a small town in New York, Nick had just moved to Los Angeles with a handful of songs. He wound up teaching them to his new bandmates and recording them in the evening at a professional studio in the backyard of a home where his friend was house-sitting.

Everything went according to plan until the last night

“We worked from 5pm until 9am for three days,” he recalls. “On the final day, the girl called us and said, ‘You’ve got to get out of there. The owner is on the way’. We cleaned up, grabbed our gear, and left. As we were pulling out, this woman pulled into the driveway. However, we forgot to dump our work onto an external,” he laughs. “Our buddy snuck back in at 2am, stayed in the dark, and transferred the songs. When he got home, he threw his fist in the air with the external! That really started our process of learning how to be a band and producers.”

Long established for his chameleonic proficiency, Amtrac spent the last decade proving himself with melodic house tracks, infectious indie dance hooks and everything in between. events.description:
The Music of Hey Arnold! Live featuring Jim Lang & The PS 118 AllStars celebrates the 30th anniversary of one of television's most cherished animated series.

Led by award winning composer Jim Lang, best known for his unforgettable theme music, original songs, and score for Hey Arnold!, this one of a kind concert brings the music of the series to life on stage. Blending jazz, hip hop, blues, R&B and funk, Lang created a sound unlike anything else on television, helping give Hey Arnold! its heart, warmth, humor and soul. Thirty years later, the music continues to connect with fans of all ages and inspire musicians around the world.

Performed by Jim Lang and The PS 118 AllStars, the evening features the show's unforgettable themes, fan favorite songs, and some of the moments that made Hey Arnold! so special. Accompanied by multimedia visuals and stories from behind the music, the performance also includes a special guest appearance by series creator Craig Bartlett.

Whether you grew up with Hey Arnold! or are discovering its music for the first time, this 30th anniversary celebration is a chance to experience one of animation's most distinctive and enduring scores performed live by the composer who created it.

events.address: 50 Mark West Springs Road, Santa Rosa, CA, 95403
events.description:
For 58 years, Tower of Power has delivered the best in funk and soul music. East Bay Grease defined their sound and landed them with Warner Brothers. Bump City, their 1972 debut for the label, was a hit on both the Billboard 200 and the R&B Albums. The 70s were a boom period with radio classics like “So Very Hard to Go” and “What Is Hip,” and the band continued to tour and record over the years. Fifty years later, in 2018, they returned to Oakland to celebrate their landmark 50th anniversary. Tower’s window-rattling grooves and raucous party spirit had been a balm for the soul throughout their half-century existence.

The band has traveled the world, enjoying hit singles on their own and backing legendary artists, including Otis Redding, Elton John, Santana, the Grateful Dead, John Lee Hooker, Aerosmith, Bonnie Raitt, and countless others. In the process they’ve defined an “Oakland soul” sound as instantly recognizable as those from Castillo’s hometown, Detroit, as well as inspirations like Memphis and Philadelphia.

events.title: New People: An Eye for an Eye
events.description:
This screening will take place at NEW PEOPLE CINEMA, located at 1746 Post Street in Japantown.

Director Tanaz Eshaghian in person for a post-screening Q&A

An Eye for an Eye unfolds like a real-life courtroom thriller, with stakes as high as life and death. Years after killing her abusive husband in an act of self-defense, Tahereh now faces execution unless she can pay the Diya—blood money demanded by her abuser’s family. With the clock ticking and public sympathy running low, her son Mohsen is thrust into a desperate race against time to save his mother’s life, turning to outside donors in a society where victims of domestic abuse are often met with silence—or scorn. With unprecedented access to private negotiations, legal proceedings, and intimate family moments, the filmmakers bring us deep inside a harrowing moral and legal labyrinth. We witness not only the emotional toll on Tahereh and her children, but also the chilling mechanics of a justice system shaped by patriarchal values and religious law. Gripping and deeply human, An Eye for an Eye lays bare the personal costs of systemic injustice—and the fierce resilience of a family fighting for their right to move forward.

His virtuosity on the guitar is matched only by his prolific compositional skills, which have generated numerous original works spanning multiple albums including “Confessions of Deprived Youth” (1991) and “Via Zammata” (2015). Another Planet Entertainment presents

Cameron Winter at Carnegie Hall
Directed by Paul Thomas Anderson
Presented in 35mm

Wednesday, December 2 | The Castro

Cameron Winter, in December 2025, after a months-long sold-out tour with his band Geese, returned to New York to play a single show at Carnegie Hall. This is the movie.

Directed and shot on 35mm and 16mm by Oscar-winning filmmaker Paul Thomas Anderson (One Battle After Another), the crew includes filmmaker and actor Benny Safdie (The Smashing Machine) and music producer Ariel Rechtshaid (Grammy winner for albums with Vampire Weekend and Adele).

GQ praised Cameron Winter’s show at Carnegie Hall as “staggeringly good,” and Nick Cave said he has a “a glorious, emotive voice with brilliant, blistering words, a racked and wondrous thing.” Winter’s solo album Heavy Metal was named one of the best of the year by Pitchfork, Rolling Stone, Paste and Mojo and Geese’s last record Getting Killed was named the best album of 2025 by The New Yorker, NME, and Stereogum.

| Performances: December 2-3, 2026 |

A holiday mash-up for the whole family, The Hip Hop Nutcracker returns for another spectacular tour. Directed and choreographed by Tony and Olivier Award-nominated Jennifer Weber, this contemporary dance spectacle is a re-mixed and re-imagined version of the classic, smashing hip hop dance and Tchaikovsky’s timeless music together into a heart-stirring and inspirational holiday event. The Hip Hop Nutcracker is brought to life by a powerhouse cast of a dozen all-star dancers, a DJ, a violinist, and MC Kurtis Blow, one of hip hop’s founding fathers, who opens the show with a short set.

Just like the original, in The Hip Hop Nutcracker, Maria-Clara and the Nutcracker Prince go on a dream adventure battling a gang of mice, visiting the land of sweets and learning the lessons of the holiday season. Innovative digital graffiti and visuals transform the landscape of E.T.A. Hoffmann’s beloved story from traditional 19th Century Germany to the vibrant, diverse sights and sounds of contemporary New York City.

Grab your family and friends and let the dynamic performers of The Hip Hop Nutcracker take you on a journey that celebrates love, community and the magic of the holiday season.

Jeremiah Chiu is a synthesist in the broadest sense of the word—a craftsperson of the modular synth and other musical instruments and tools, as well as an artist, designer, and educator whose work continually brings disparate forms of knowledge into new relationships. While widely recognized for his versatile electronic music as a solo artist, textured recordings in a duo with violist Marta Sofia Honer, and the experimental quintet he co-leads, SML, Chiu has simultaneously maintained a practice as a graphic designer and visual artist, developing a practice attentive to both the structure of technological systems and the contingencies of liveness and emergence.

For Chiu, visual thinking and musical thinking are not separate disciplines but different expressions of the same innate compositional sensibility. This point of view is born equally from his idiosyncratic sense of aesthetics and his capacity for a warm and porous exchange within a thriving community of creative collaborators that stretches between Chicago and Los Angeles.

Rooted in Chicago's deeply interconnected experimental music community, his music has consistently developed through long-term collaborations and shared artistic inquiry. events.description:
The past three decades have written a story packed full of surreal experiences, epic moments, groundbreaking involvement and huge accomplishments. The String Cheese Incident has been recognized for their commitment to musical creativity and integrity, for their community spirit, philanthropic endeavors, and for their innovative approach to the business of music.

When The String Cheese Incident’s growth first started gaining momentum in the 1990s, as the Internet was just beginning to take hold and the major-label business model was failing, the band decided to make music on their own terms.

Since then, The String Cheese Incident has gone on to carve out a completely unique approach to the business of music; they are truly pioneers of a new way of “making a band.” With the Internet as their tool, SCI was among the first artists to disseminate information online, such as tour dates, release information, and other news, to their growing fan base. Rather than doing business on such terms as “the bottom line,” SCI put their music and their fans first, opening companies of their own, including a ticketing company, a merchandise company and a fan travel agency, to best serve their community. The band’s record label, SCI Fidelity Records, has always operated under the same ideals. Even early on, SCI Fidelity embraced downloadable music and file sharing, delivering SCI’s “On The Road” series, where every show the band plays is made available for download on the Internet. events.title: 10% Off: “Tapas Tuesdays” in Union Square
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerBota Tapas & Paella Bar near Downtown San Francisco and Union Square is doing “Tapas Tuesdays” and enjoy all of our delicious Spanish Tapas at 10% Off. Just mention “Tapas Tuesday” to our server before ordering to get the discount.
About Bota Tapas and Paella Bar

As an age-old tradition dating back to the early 1800s, Spanish travelers used “BOTA”, or traditional sheep-skinned repositories, to transport and share their wine. The Spaniards historically thrived on the values of sharing and community: two ideals that have buoyantly withstood the test of time. Tailored around these same ideals are Spain’s cuisine and the development of “tapas,” style dining – where individuals share small plates and memories. From Seville to San Francisco, and across the world, our goal is to initiate more memories – this is why and how we operate. Whether it be with your friends or family, we here at Bota sincerely hope that you enjoy this stop on your journey.

The program runs 5 to 8 p.m. and focuses on fiscal management, budgeting, investment strategies, and resources to help women artists build toward financial security and wealth. An interactive audience session follows the panel, then a networking reception with refreshments sponsored by Schwab Corporation.
The panelists bring substantial experience in starting businesses, running an art practice as a business, and building wealth:

Sheila Cunningham is an executive and business coach. Her focus is teaching practical tools which give businesses a solid grasp of financials, organizational management, and sales processes to increase profitability for small businesses. Sheila’s career has been spent studying successful and unsuccessful businesses as a reporter and editor at BusinessWeek magazine, as well as spending ten years in entrepreneurial ventures. Sheila is Trustee and Treasurer of the Mechanics’ Institute and a member of the Financial Women of San Francisco.

events.title: “March to Ballhalla” SF’s Pier 48 to Thrive City for Valkyries Playoff Watch Party (4-6p)
events.address: 402 Terry A Francois Blvd., San Francisco, CA
events.description:
Submitted by the Event Organizer2026 Valkyries Free WNBA Playoff Watch Party at Thrive City (SF)Valkyries fans will gather at Pier 48 for the first-ever March to Ballhalla ahead of the team’s first away game of the 2026 WNBA Playoffs, presented by Kaiser Permanente.
The march will begin at Pier 48 Lot A, migrate along Terry Francois Blvd, and end at Thrive City for the Valkyries Playoffs Watch Party, presented by Kaiser Permanente. T
he march will feature music by the Fremont High School Marching Band, city officials including San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie, Valkyries staff, fans, and community organizations such as the Lowrider Council. Ari Waller will emcee and Valkyries Bestie Violet will be hyping up marchers and meeting with fans.

events.description: Submitted by the Event OrganizerIs art political? Of course, it is! From the brush strokes to the paint colors to the pen nib, everything is political! events.title: Filmscreening: Punking Punk
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerPunk promised that anyone could get on a stage. It didn’t always keep the promise. These two documentaries follow the people who held it to its word: the women who founded the first all-female bands in Düsseldorf, West Berlin, and Zurich, and the queer punks who built a scene of their own when the movement’s macho turn pushed them out. Two films, one evening, and the same refusal to ask permission.
Einfach machen! She-Punks von 1977 bis heute
Reto Caduff, Germany/Switzerland 2024, 94 min, German with English subtitles

“Do it! Don’t talk about it. Do it!” Martina Weith, lead singer and saxophonist of Germany’s first all-female punk band Östro 430, summed up the movement’s radical practice in a single demand. Decades later, the women who led pioneering bands like Mania D, Malaria!, and Kleenex are back on stage, decrying patriarchy, sexual repression, dogmatic feminism, and right-wing violence with the same electric fervor. Caduff’s nervy documentary traces the story of the women of German-language punk — innovators and provocateurs who fought as hard against bourgeois society as against the subculture’s own machismo. With interviews from Weith, Gudrun Gut, and Bettina Köster, it looks back on punk’s contradictory gender dynamics and these women’s triumphant fight to plant their own black flag within it.
Queercore: How to Punk a Revolution
Yony Leyser, Germany/USA 2017, 83 min, in English
While some of punk’s brashest arms-bearers were enjoying...

events.title: Fruit Bats
events.description: Submitted by the Event OrganizerThe midwest, particularly the part of the midwest Eric D. Johnson hails from, is a largely flat expanse. Zipping through it on the highway, you’ll see cities and towns rise up in the distance, but blink and you’ll miss other man-made rejoinders to horizontal living dotting the landscape, hill after hill, built from the refuse of the past: landfills. Some of these hills make for great sledding spots, parks, and trails. Others turn organic waste into compost. The Landfill, Fruit Bats’ June 12, 2026 album from Merge Records, is something else entirely: a mountain dominating the landscape of Johnson’s heart.

Submitted by the Event OrganizerNico Larson is a California singer-songwriter and the lead singer, pianist, and guitarist of the band Próxima Parada. He writes vulnerable songs centered on personal growth and human connection.
Próxima Parada means “next stop” in Spanish and Portuguese. While riding the bus in their hometown of San Luis Obispo, California, Nico and his bandmates would hear at every stop, “Now approaching, próxima parada…” After years of touring the U.S. and moving from one next stop to another, the band has developed an uplifting, groove-driven sound that explores embracing who we are while working toward who we’re becoming. Their music blends elements of soul, R&B, folk, and indie rock.

For this solo performance, Nico will share Próxima Parada’s songs in their original form, just as he first wrote them: alone at the piano.

events.title: Free Parenting Workshop: Decode Your Child’s Behavior (Mill Valley)
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerBehind the Behavior: Understanding Your Child at Every Developmental Stage and What You Might See at Home
Friday, October 2, 2026
9:00-10:00 a.m. / Marin Horizon School Library
When we think about the beginning of the school year, we think about new teachers, new friends, new expectations, and all of the logistics of parenting a school-aged child. And then comes the push for more independence, the nightly meltdown that didn’t happen last year, or the “please don’t talk to me in front of my friends.” We may find ourselves wondering what happened and how did we get here? It’s easy to feel lost when our children enter a new developmental stage. We may understand what to expect from a parenting book or article, but it can be much harder to recognize and respond to these changes when they show up at home. In this workshop, we’ll explore the developmental stages of the elementary and middle school years, what to expect as children grow and change, and practical ways to navigate these new phases while strengthening communication, connection, and understanding with your child.

events.title: Carlos Motta: When Time Stands Still
events.venue: Institute of the Arts and Sciences
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerCarlos Motta’s When Time Stands Still, the artist’s second solo show with the IAS, features new and recent installations, videos, and sculptures highlighting the artist’s preoccupation with the historical and aesthetic productions of difference and marginalization that shape the present.
The selection of artworks in the exhibition explore the unsettling experience of living in a time that seems violently stuck on repeat. Archetypal figures from art history (a fool, a siren, a witness, a victim) reappear in the current moment as containers of time, bringing the past of imperialism, colonization, and displacement into a present marked by the rise of anti-immigration politics, climate injustice, and other forms of disposability. Some works challenge this violent repetition of time. The clock moves, if gruelingly, in an endurance-based video performance, No One, 2025. For forty-six minutes, the artist undertakes to keep his eyes open, witnessing, withstanding, confronting, and resisting the bombardment of images, both historical and otherwise, that normalize harm. In another video work, Gravity, 2024, performers enact rescue carries, supporting each other until they can’t bear the weight. Together, the artworks act as a proposal about how to rethink time—how to slow time—with a poetic and aesthetic cadence that might counter the numbing reverberations of living in the present.
