Bring the whole family to the San Mateo County History Museum on Saturday, November 7, for HISTORY IN MOTION, a FREE Grand Opening Celebration filled with history, music, discovery and fun!
Be among the first to explore three exciting new experiences: discover historic carriages and automobiles in the Taube Family Carriage House and Automobile Gallery, travel millions of years into the Peninsula’s past in the H.E.R.O. events.description: Presidio TrustJoin us at the Presidio Tunnel Tops for a family-friendly Día de los Muertos & Diwali event in the park. Celebrated annually in the fall season, these two distinct cultural observances come together in a national park to honor South Asian and Latinx traditions. Designed intentionally as a celebration and a learning opportunity, attendees are invited to participate in a wide range of activities that include arts and crafts, storytelling, cultural dance, song, and a fire ceremony, and learn about social and environmental justice issues in both cultures.

Show description: Francesca, a contemporary American filmmaker, is shooting a documentary on a newly excavated fresco in Pompeii said to provide startling evidence about sex and the sacred. Japanese Tea Garden
The Japanese Tea Garden provides visitors from around the world with an opportunity to experience the natural beauty, tranquility, and harmony of a Japanese-style garden in the heart of San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park.
Originally created as a “Japanese Village” exhibit for the 1894 California Midwinter International Exposition, the Japanese Tea Garden endures as one of the most popular attractions in San Francisco, featuring classic elements such as an arched drum bridge, pagodas, stone lanterns, stepping stone paths, native Japanese plants, serene koi ponds, and a zen garden. Cherry blossom trees bloom throughout the garden in March and April.
Admission to the Japanese Tea Garden is free for San Francisco residents with valid ID. Free hours for everyone (even non-residents) are 9-10 am every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

events.title: Echoes of the Seasons: A Piano Dialogue Between East and West
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerSFPLExplore how Eastern and Western composers interpret the seasons across different musical traditions. Western selections express vivid natural imagery, from Vivaldi’s dynamic storms to Tchaikovsky’s romantic winter scenes and the reflective mood of Autumn Leaves. These works translate the physical world into sound through color, emotion and narrative.
Eastern musical philosophy centers Yijing (意境), an aesthetic that blends atmosphere, poetry and spiritual resonance. Rooted in the Chinese pentatonic scale, this approach moves beyond direct depiction, inviting listeners to experience nature as a contemplative reflection of the self.

Through classical masterworks, jazz and traditional Chinese repertoire, this lecture‑recital highlights how artistic languages encounter one another across cultures. The program invites audiences to hear how different musical philosophies interpret the seasons and how these perspectives generate deeper understanding of memory, place and expression.

Japanese Tea Garden
The Japanese Tea Garden provides visitors from around the world with an opportunity to experience the natural beauty, tranquility, and harmony of a Japanese-style garden in the heart of San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park.
Originally created as a “Japanese Village” exhibit for the 1894 California Midwinter International Exposition, the Japanese Tea Garden endures as one of the most popular attractions in San Francisco, featuring classic elements such as an arched drum bridge, pagodas, stone lanterns, stepping stone paths, native Japanese plants, serene koi ponds, and a zen garden. Cherry blossom trees bloom throughout the garden in March and April.
Admission to the Japanese Tea Garden is free for San Francisco residents with valid ID. Free hours for everyone (even non-residents) are 9-10 am every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

The free PresidiGo Shuttle system welcomes park visitors, residents, and employees with fully accessible shuttles and bike racks.
There are two PresidiGo Shuttle services, each with different policies and guidelines – Around the Park and Downtown.

Downtown (Free on Weekends)
The Downtown express route make stops at the Presidio Transit Center on the Main Post, the Letterman District, Union Street/Van Ness Avenue, Embarcadero BART, and the Transbay Terminal.
The shuttle operates from 5:45 am to 9:30 pm on weekdays and 10 am to 7:30 pm on weekends. On weekdays, during the evening commute (leaving the Presidio only) from 4-7:40 pm, a valid MUNI Passport (not a MUNI Fast Pass) is required. No pass is required on weekends.
It’s free for Presidio Employees and Residents every day with an appropriate boarding pass. Connecting service to Caltrain is available.
The Downtown PresidiGo does not operate on federal holidays.
Around the Park (Every Day – 2 Routes)
Around the Park is free and available to visitors, residents, and employees all day. The shuttle runs two continuous 30-minute loops:

The Crissy Field Route serves the northern Presidio including the Main Post, Golden Gate Bridge, Fort Scott and Letterman District

Every third Saturday, you are invited to bicycle with the San Francisco Midnight Mystery Ride as they set out to a new mystery location in SF.

events.title: San Francisco Bike Party (First Fridays)
events.description:
San Francisco Bike Party (First Fridays)
San Francisco Bike Party
San Francisco Bike Party (not to be confused with Critical Mass) is a monthly celebration of biking for riders of different ages, types, and skill levels to enjoy. Every month is a different theme and you’re encouraged to dress up.
San Francisco Bike Party is held on the first Friday at 8:00 pm every month (meet at 7:30p, roll at 8p). The starting location and route also changes every month. Check SF Bike Party’s Facebook page for updates.
The rides are fun and safe with stops to dance and socialize along the way. You’ll follow planned routes exploring all different parts of the city each month. They encourage people to bring positivity and contribute to good times while being respectful to others.

Who runs it? Created by a co-op, by and for bike enthusiasts, run by volunteers who plan the routes, test ride them, help participants ride in control, avoid traffic disruption, and not get lost. How SFBP rides: – Stay in the right lane – Stop at red lights – Leave no trace – Ride predictably and in control – Roll past conflict – Ride prepared – When in doubt, “bike party!!”

events.title: Drawing From Film—Night of the Hunter
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerSFPLWe’ll be pausing Laughton’s Southern Gothic thriller, Night of the Hunter, to draw striking frames. We’ll be focusing on the art deco design, dramatic shadows and poses in the film.
Basic materials (pencils, paper, erasers) will be provided. You may bring your own materials, but please no fume-creating paint or paint pens. Watercolor, ink and gouache are fine.

This is a self-led event; there will be no instruction or feedback. However, there will be an opportunity at the end of the session to look at others’ drawings and show your own.
PG, 92 mins., 1955. Closed captions (CC) in English. Due to pauses for drawing, the full film will not be shown.
The event takes places in the Main Library at 100 Larkin Street, in the Latino/Hispanic Meeting Room.

La Peña Cultural Center
This free, participatory event has been a staple at La Peña Cultural Center for 12 years due to its incredible fun, and recurs every 1st and 3rd Sunday of each month.
Come enjoy the Afro-Cuban folkloric drums, dances, and songs of rumba. Rumba is the word used for a group of related, community-oriented, music and dance styles in Cuba.
Rumba developed in rural Cuba, with strong influences from African drumming and Spanish poetry and singing.

Come play, sing, dance, or simply watch and enjoy.

Kim Shuck was San Francisco’s seventh Poet Laureate. Her poetry draws on her multiethnic background which includes Polish and Cherokee heritage, and her experiences as a lifelong resident of San Francisco. Her most recent book of poetry, November Dance Shirt, was published in 2026, and her book of essays, Noodle, Rant, Tangent, was published in 2022. The free PresidiGo Shuttle system welcomes park visitors, residents, and employees with fully accessible shuttles and bike racks.
There are two PresidiGo Shuttle services, each with different policies and guidelines – Around the Park and Downtown.

Downtown (Free on Weekends)
The Downtown express route make stops at the Presidio Transit Center on the Main Post, the Letterman District, Union Street/Van Ness Avenue, Embarcadero BART, and the Transbay Terminal.
The shuttle operates from 5:45 am to 9:30 pm on weekdays and 10 am to 7:30 pm on weekends. On weekdays, during the evening commute (leaving the Presidio only) from 4-7:40 pm, a valid MUNI Passport (not a MUNI Fast Pass) is required. No pass is required on weekends.
It’s free for Presidio Employees and Residents every day with an appropriate boarding pass. Connecting service to Caltrain is available.
The Downtown PresidiGo does not operate on federal holidays.
Around the Park (Every Day – 2 Routes)
Around the Park is free and available to visitors, residents, and employees all day. The shuttle runs two continuous 30-minute loops:

The Crissy Field Route serves the northern Presidio including the Main Post, Golden Gate Bridge, Fort Scott and Letterman District

Critical Mass is a mass bicycle ride that takes place on the last Friday of each month in San Francisco. Meet and 6pm, ride at 6:30 pm from Embarcadero Plaza (foot of Market Street) and in cities around the world. Everyone is invited. No one is in charge. Bring your bike.
Please Note: Critical Mass tends to practice extreme bike power by taking to the streets and riding in the car lanes causing endless annoyance to motorists.
In San Francisco especially, this event can get HUGE. Consider this is fair warning to stay away from driving in the downtown SF area on the last Friday of every month.

events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerCuban Rumba Jam: Play, Sing, Dance & Enjoy | Berkeley
La Peña Cultural Center
This free, participatory event has been a staple at La Peña Cultural Center for 12 years due to its incredible fun, and recurs every 1st and 3rd Sunday of each month.
Come enjoy the Afro-Cuban folkloric drums, dances, and songs of rumba. Rumba is the word used for a group of related, community-oriented, music and dance styles in Cuba.
Rumba developed in rural Cuba, with strong influences from African drumming and Spanish poetry and singing.

Come play, sing, dance, or simply watch and enjoy.

events.title: Keepin' It Safe in the City
events.description:
Happening at Civic Center Plaza, the 3rd annual Keepin’ It Safe in the City features fire trucks, a bounce house, music and food. Attendees will also meet first responders, take part in fun activities and win raffle prizes.
Sponsored by: The San Francisco District Attorney’s Office
More information here.
Also be sure the check out the adjacent Fall Family Festival and Market Street Arts & Theater Festival.

events.title: Market Street Arts & Theater Festival
events.description:
Taking place at location in Mid Market and Civic Center, on October 17th, the Market Street Arts & Theater Festival, 4-10pm, will feature of an evening of entertainment. In Civic Center, UN Plaza will host circus and aerial dance performances by:
Dear San Francisco
Circus Bella
Spectrum Theater
The Peoples Circus
Bandaloop Vertical Dancers
ACT’S Young Conservatory Cabaret

At Civic Center Plaza don’t miss Dueling Pianos. Also stop by Limoncello for drinks and bites.

More about their full event here.

Also check out adjacent kid and family friendly events: Fall Family Festival in Fulton Plaza, 4-7pm & Keepin’ It Safe the City in Civic Center Plaza, 10am-2pm.

events.title: Fall Family Festival
events.description:
Taking place under the twinkling Spectra lights, the Fall Family Festival on October 17th, from 4 to 7pm; features fun carnival games, free pumpkin decorating, face painting, the San Francisco Public Library Bookmobile, and entertainment such as stilt walkers and bubble magic with Sterling Bubble.
The selfie station with the autumn-themed Petalz Flower Truck is a must stop photo op with City Hall as the backdrop, as are the carnival treats: cotton candy, candy apples and local food trucks featuring fall fair favorites.
Sign up on Eventbrite for an event day reminder, but no ticket needed to attend this free event.
This event is sponsored by: Avenue Greenlight, an investment engine for San Francisco’s community projects, providing high-impact grants with tangible results; along with Civic Center Community Benefit District, Illuminate, the San Francisco Public Library and San Francisco Recreation & Parks Department.

Also be sure to check out adjacent kid & family events, San Francisco District Attorney’s Office‘s Keepin’ It Safe in the City (Civic Center Plaza, 10am-2pm) and Market Street Arts‘ Market Street Arts & Theater Festival (many locations, including UN Plaza, with circus and aerial performances in the evening, event runs 4-10pm).

events.title: Civic Center Pumpkin Patch from Compass Family Services
events.description: Visit the pop up pumpkin patch sprouting in Civic Center Plaza on Wednesday, October 28, 9am-4pm. From Compass Family Services, all area neighborhood kids are welcome; expect activities, treats, entertainment and, of course, pumpkins!

events.title: Holiday Season Performing Arts Showcase
events.description:
On Friday, November 13, from 5–7 p.m., Fulton Plaza will come alive beneath the dazzling Spectra lights for the Holiday Season Performing Arts Showcase, a celebration bringing together some of downtown’s most exciting performing arts organizations for one unforgettable evening.
Guests will be treated to a dynamic lineup of live performances of what’s on stage this season. Expect short works from the San Francisco Opera, San Francisco Ballet, the African American Shakespeare Company, the San Francisco Philharmonic and RAW Dance, and more. From powerful voices and sweeping orchestral music to captivating movement and theatrical performances, the showcase offers a little bit of everything — and is a memorable way to launch the holiday season.
This event is free, and no ticket required to attend.
Also be sure to visit the adjacent food trucks and bar, and visit with the arts organizations to learn more about what they’re bringing to the stage Fall 2026-Winter 2027.

events.title: Civic Center Plaza Tree Lighting 2026
events.description:
Save the date! The annual Civic Center Plaza Tree Lighting is taking place across the street from an illuminated City Hall on Wednesday, December 2nd, 4-7pm! Featuring a night of festive entertainment, a toy giveaway for the first 500 children, “snow” flurries, holiday beverages and bites for purchase and more. Also the night wouldn’t be complete without a visit from the VIP-of-the-hour: Santa!
More information to come.

events.title: Quinteto Latino
events.address: Yerba Buena Gardens, Mission St. between 3rd & 4th Sts., San Francisco, CA, 94103, United States
events.description:
A wind quintet with an imperative mission, Quinteto Latino is a singular Bay Area-based chamber ensemble devoted to breaking down the racial and social barriers that have long plagued the classical music world. Spotlighting and performing compositions by artists of Latin American heritage, the quintet’s acclaimed musicians are devoted to building community through classical music, performance and advocacy. With concerts featuring expertly melded flute, oboe, clarinet, French horn and bassoon, QL brings out the vibrant colors and vigorous rhythms of Latin American music. The group’s programs include arrangements of beloved Latino folk melodies and contemporary works by illustrious composers such as Gabriela Lena Frank, Orlando Jacinto García and Paquito D’Rivera, including many commissioned by the ensemble.

Supported in part by the Alice M. Ditson Fund of Columbia University.

events.title: Follow the Music
events.address: Yerba Buena Gardens, Mission St. between 3rd & 4th Sts., San Francisco, CA, 94103, United States
events.description:
Free RSVP
Since launching in 2023 Follow the Music has been at the forefront of a rising movement promoting arts education around the Bay Area. The nonprofit organization introduces its next phase with an emerging artists music festival designed to showcase aspiring young musicians. Bringing families and young people from all over the region to the urban oasis of the Gardens, Follow the Music celebrates the Bay Area’s unrivaled cultural heritage by building a bridge between that legacy and the young people carrying it forward. Featuring musicians ages 14-25, the event includes musicians from the San Francisco Community Music Center, Oakland School for the Arts, SFJAZZ, GLIDE Memorial Church, Blue Bear School of Music, Elevate Oakland, Enriching Lives Through Music and other organizations. Drawing on the Bay Area’s cultural diversity, the lineup crosses genres from classical and jazz to soul, rock and Latin jazz. It also features guest speakers from music, sports and popular culture, emceed by Maya Hernandez from KEXP. A community resource fair provides families and students with opportunities to connect directly with many Bay Area music education programs while learning about classes and scholarships. The muse can take many pathways and Follow the Music is here to ensure that all are open.

events.title: YBG Dance Day
events.address: Yerba Buena Gardens, Mission St. between 3rd & 4th Sts., San Francisco, CA, 94103, United States
events.description:
Free RSVP
A party, a workout, a meditation and a communal celebration, Yerba Buena Gardens Dance Day is a portal to a joyous dance-filled world! Presented by YBG Festival and Rhythm & Motion, YBG Dance Day transforms the Gardens into an outdoor dance heaven where participants can sample dance in a variety of forms and flavors with some of the Bay Area’s most talented teachers. Classes are one-hour long and span a wide range of dance genres. Whether you are new to dance or a seasoned professional, Yerba Buena Gardens Dance Day is open to everyone! Bring comfortable shoes, a water bottle and your curiosity for movement – stay for an hour or the full day. Invite friends and family. This is your day to dance!
This year, Dance Day honors the life and legacy of Rhythm & Motion founder Consuelo Faust (1953-2025). We celebrate the spirit she championed – living the belief that anyone can dance and that dance has the power to bring people together in joy. Following the day of classes, there will be a celebratory music and dance performance that uplifts her vision and the vibrant SF Bay Area dance community she deeply loved and helped to nurture throughout her life.

events.title: San Francisco Indigenous Peoples Day with special performance by Jeremy Dutcher
events.address: Yerba Buena Gardens, Mission St. between 3rd & 4th Sts., San Francisco, CA, 94103, United States
events.description:
Free RSVP
Join us in celebration of San Francisco Indigenous Peoples Day with a magnificent profusion of Native American art, music and vendors. The event highlights the vastly diverse and talented community of Indigenous artists in the Bay Area, California and the Americas. Presented on Yelamu, Ramaytush Ohlone Territory, in partnership with the International Indian Treaty Council, the program at Yerba Buena Gardens follows the Annual Indigenous Peoples Day Sunrise Gathering on Alcatraz – please check the IITC website for updates. Schedule to be announced.

A groundbreaking Indigenous musician whose art flows directly out of his cultural activism, tenor Jeremy Dutcher is a conservatory-trained Canadian composer, musicologist and performer who has turned European classical music into a vehicle for language preservation. A member of Neqotkuk First Nation in Eastern Canada now based in Montréal, Québec, Dutcher catapulted to renown with his debut album Wolastoqiyik Lintuwakonawa, which won the 2018 Polaris Music Prize and the Juno Award for Indigenous Music Album of the Year at the Canadian equivalent of the Grammys in 2019. The project unearthed century-old archival recordings of his ancestors, which he turned into collaborative compositions on piano. Sung entirely in Wolastoqey, his endangered mother tongue, the album led to collaborations with artists such as Yo-Yo Ma and Feist. events.title: Richard Howell’s John Coltrane Tribute
events.address: Yerba Buena Gardens, Mission St. between 3rd & 4th Sts., San Francisco, CA, 94103, United States
events.description: The 100th anniversary of John Coltrane’s birthday has inspired dozens of performances across the Bay Area this year, but no artist is better equipped to evoke the legacy of the saxophone titan and spiritual seeker than Richard Howell. An acclaimed musician, composer and educator, he defines his performances as “Bridge Music,” a jazz pathway that creates sonic connection across obstacles and differences. It’s music that celebrates diversity as it bridges, unites and merges the experience of all listeners, an approach rooted in the spirit of John Coltrane’s “A Love Supreme.” Howell, who spent years on the road with Etta James, also embraces the contradiction of James Brown’s simple yet intricate African-inspired rhythmic concepts and the deep soulfulness of the Isley Brothers. As a saxophonist and vocalist, he has a gift for connecting to multi-generational audiences with an abiding spirituality that invites all listeners to partake. He’s particularly eager to present an afternoon honoring the spirit and music of John Coltrane, he explains. “I’ve had the blessing of a close relationship with his son, Ravi Coltrane, as my son Elé has been part of Ravi’s rhythm section as a drummer for the past seven years. What I’m envisioning is an acoustic jazz quartet – tenor saxophone, acoustic piano, bass and drums – rooted in the Coltrane tradition, but also reflecting the living continuum of that music.”

events.title: Joe Bataan
events.address: Yerba Buena Gardens, Mission St. between 3rd & 4th Sts., San Francisco, CA, 94103, United States
events.description:
Free RSVP
Opening Set from MeloDious

Festival favorite Joe Bataan, a Latin music legend since the mid-1960s, returns to the Gardens for his third performance in the past four years. He made an indelible mark as one of the early stars of Fania Records with a seductive combination of doo-wop vocals and boogaloo, one of the era’s defining sounds. Born Bataan Nitollano to a Filipino father and African-American mother and raised in Spanish Harlem, he is the father of the Latin soul sound, crooning hits like “Gypsy Woman” and “Ordinary Guy.” But Bataan never stayed in one groove for long. He went on to expand his sound in the ’70s with his Ghetto Records releases, co-coining the apt moniker “salsoul,” though he adapted to changing currents at the end of the decade with forays into disco and hip-hop (scoring the early rap hit “Rap-O Clap-O” in 1979). Stepping back from performing in the early ‘80s, he largely disappeared from the scene while working as a youth counselor in detention facilities. It’s a dramatic story that he recounts with humor and searing detail in his 2024 memoir Streetology: The Legacy of the Afro-Filipino, King of Latin Soul. Since returning to music in 2005, he’s reclaimed his crown and is still going strong in his 80s, a fact made evident by his triumphant YBG Festival performances.

events.title: Afro-Filipino Jazz Project
events.address: Yerba Buena Gardens, Mission St. between 3rd & 4th Sts., San Francisco, CA, 94103, United States
events.description:
Free RSVP
Few artists have appeared at the Festival more frequently than flutist, percussionist and arranger John Calloway. Whether he’s leading his own band, performing in the sextet of longtime creative partner John Santos, or directing the Latin Jazz Youth Ensemble of San Francisco, Calloway is a Bay Area icon who’s been at the center of the San Francisco Latin jazz scene for some five decades. But his latest and most personal project yet, the Afro-Filipino Jazz Project, takes his music in a new direction. Founded in 2022 as a creative, interactive space, the Project is intended to bring together Afro Filipinx, African American and Filipino American musicians to explore a broad range of musical styles, with a particular emphasis on jazz idioms, African American roots and traditional and folkloric Filipino music. It’s one component of the larger Afro-Filipino Project, a platform dedicated to highlighting and celebrating, individually and collectively, the art practices and artists of the African American and Filipino American communities whose contributions have profoundly shaped our nation’s artistic narrative. For this performance the AFJP features bass star Marcus Shelby, inveterately grooving drummer Deszon Claiborne, Latin jazz piano specialist Murray Low, saxophonist TJ Milan, Conrad Benedicto on kulintang, vocalist and dancer Ting Alvarez and guest vocalist Anna Maria Flechero.

events.title: Bhangra & Beats Night Market
events.address: Yerba Buena Gardens, Mission St. between 3rd & 4th Sts., San Francisco, CA, 94103, United States
events.description:
San Francisco’s biggest South Asian celebration is back, and for the first time ever, it lands at Yerba Buena Gardens, one of downtown’s most iconic arts and cultural destinations.
On July 24 and November 13, Yerba Buena Gardens, Jessie Square, and Yerba Buena Lane will transform into a vibrant, open-air celebration of music, dance, food, and culture—bringing together community, creativity, and connection in the heart of downtown.
As the only outdoor celebration of its size and scale in the Bay Area dedicated to South Asian culture, Bhangra & Beats continues to create a space that is both rooted in tradition and alive with the energy of the Bay.
At the heart of it all is the vibrant Bhangra & Beats atmosphere, a family-friendly celebration where traditional Punjabi rhythms meet Bay Area energy. Non Stop Bhangra collective will once again lead the experience with its signature mix of interactive dance lessons, beautiful performances, live dhol drumming, DJs, and an open dance floor, all flowing into a lively marketplace with food vendors, local makers, community activations, restaurant and bar specials, and family-friendly activities.
Come for the music, stay for the energy. Whether you’re dancing, eating, shopping, or just taking it all in, there’s something here for everyone.
